mergedPulls.title: server,daemon(#1493): model fallback chain + provider circuit breaker
mergedPulls.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xiechimon"} -->
_Requested by **ian** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WRVEp3Ljey1pvjthhYAqdU?thread=cmsg_01WRVEp3Ljey1pvjthhYAqdUCMT9qmYV8aygZrr2st25L3)_

## What

Adds a model fallback chain and a per-provider circuit breaker (#1493). Design choices are recorded in the [ticket comment](https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1493#issuecomment-6340370385) and in `docs/spec/11`.

- `agent.fallbackModels`: ordered `{provider, modelId}` list, max 5, null by default. Set through POST and PATCH `/api/teams/:id/agents`. An agent without it never switches models.
- When a plan or build step fails because quota ran out, the model returned 404, or the model key failed authentication, `finishStep` calls `planModelFallback` (`services/model-fallback.ts`). The step goes back to pending on the next fallback that passes the home machine's runtime gate, is not a dead model, and whose provider the breaker allows. `step.fallback` records the current model and the models already tried. The same model is never tried twice on one step. When the chain runs out, the existing paths run unchanged (quota goes to waiting_quota, 404 and auth go to the failure path).
- Review, verify, merge and chief steps never switch models. Their verdicts feed the merge readiness gate (ADR 0021), so a weaker model must not pass them. Rate limits (`quotaBlock.kind = capacity`) also do not switch.
- Claim payload, per-step credentials (`resolveStepCredentials`, `stepToken`), the board's waiting-for-machine chip and the step queue's blocked state all use `step.fallback.model` when set. `token_usage` therefore records the model that actually ran. Session continuation only happens between steps run on the same fallback provider. A step that switched provider starts a new session, and the task brief is injected again. Thinking level falls back to default on a fallback model.
- Each switch writes a system row to the conversation and a `model_fallback` in-app notification.
- `services/provider-health.ts`: healthy, then degraded after 3 consecutive failures, then open after 5, then half_open after 30 s with one probe step at a time (10 min lease). Success resets the provider to healthy. Quota, rate limit and auth failures count. State is in memory and resets on server restart.
- Silent success: the daemon now sends `noOutput: true` when a step succeeds with no assistant message in its transcript. A plan or build step with `noOutput` and zero tokens is retried once on the same model. A second one fails the step. Usage alone is not trusted because pi reports 0-token rows for relays that do not return usage.
- `isProviderAuthFailure` (shared) only matches messages that name an API key or `authentication_error`. Git and GitHub 401s do not trigger a switch.
- Migration `0045_model_fallback_chain` adds `agent.fallbackModels` and `step.fallback` (both nullable JSON).

The agent detail page has no editor for `fallbackModels` yet. That is left for a follow-up ticket.

## Verified

Breaker unit tests were committed before the implementation: 974fd4c (tests, red: `Cannot find module '../src/services/provider-health.js'`), then c25005d (implementation). The daemon `noOutput` test failed first (`AssertionError: expected undefined to be true`) before the runner change.

On this branch:

- Server: [server-vitest.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/555da5b51b878f9f89cb81fe23515c9a30b7f1f0/docs/verify/1493/server-vitest.txt), 3 files, 32 tests passed (provider-health, model-fallback, quota-wait).
- Daemon: [daemon-vitest.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/555da5b51b878f9f89cb81fe23515c9a30b7f1f0/docs/verify/1493/daemon-vitest.txt), 14 tests passed.
- Shared: [shared-vitest.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/555da5b51b878f9f89cb81fe23515c9a30b7f1f0/docs/verify/1493/shared-vitest.txt), 35 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --changed`: everything passed except 6 integration files that need a Playwright browser build missing from the cloud container (`chrome-headless-shell` 1243). The 3 shared JSON Schema snapshots were updated for the new fields.
- `pnpm lint` exit 0, `pnpm typecheck` exit 0, `pnpm spec:parse` PASS.
- Full e2e ran in CI: e2e (1) to (4) and e2e-gate passed on 555da5b. ebc424c merges main (conflict in `machines.ts`, both sides kept) and CI re-runs.

## Upstream

pi has `auto_retry` for transient errors on the same model and the daemon has a protocol fallback (#708). Neither switches provider or model, and neither knows the step kind, which decides whether a switch is allowed. The switch has to happen on the server, because the server holds provider keys and picks which model a claim sends. claude-agent-sdk has no cross-provider fallback.

## Risk

Two-way door for behavior: with `fallbackModels` null (every existing agent) the new code paths return early, and the quota-wait and failure paths are unchanged (quota-wait.test passes as before). The migration adds two nullable columns and is a one-way door under ADR 0021 D4, as are `services/machines.ts` and `services/credentials.ts` (security-sensitive files), so this PR needs a human merge.

/code-review (high) found 10 issues. All are fixed in a773bd7: 0-token false positives on relays that do not return usage, git 401 counted as provider auth, sessions continued across providers, a sticky `freshSession`, board and queue using the primary provider's runtime, a probe slot held after a 404, the thinking level on fallback models, notification attribution, a duplicated requeue, and a one-call helper.

/security-review: no findings. A fallback provider key is opened with `openProviderKey(todo.teamId, provider)`, so it cannot read another team's key, and `stepToken` still checks `ownedStep`. A fallback grants nothing the primary `provider` field could not already grant.

## Acceptance

- [x] Breaker state machine unit tests before implementation: 974fd4c before c25005d, [server-vitest.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/555da5b51b878f9f89cb81fe23515c9a30b7f1f0/docs/verify/1493/server-vitest.txt) (H1 to H7)
- [x] Integration: primary reports quotaBlock, step switches and is re-dispatched on the fallback: X1. All fallbacks fail, step goes to waiting_quota: X2
- [x] Negative control for steps that must not switch: X3 (review, merge), X4 (no fallbacks configured), X5 (rate limit)
- [x] Model switch visible in the conversation and notifications: X9 (system row and `model_fallback` notification rows asserted)
- [x] lint / typecheck / spec:parse / vitest related pass (see Verified)
- [x] e2e: full suite green in CI: e2e (1) to (4) and e2e-gate passed on 555da5b; the merge of main (ebc424c) re-runs them

## Issues

Closes #1493

Squash with this message:

```
server,daemon(#1493): model fallback chain + provider circuit breaker

agent.fallbackModels (ordered, max 5). Plan and build steps switch to the
next healthy fallback on quota exhaustion, model 404 or key auth failure;
review / verify / merge / chief steps never switch; rate limits do not
switch. Breaker per provider (3 degraded, 5 open, 30 s half-open probe),
in memory. Silent success (noOutput + 0 tokens) retried once.

closes #1493
```

mergedPulls.title: server, daemon: reset is the only way back to todo, a cancelled card's merge does not land, a deleted step stops (#1486, #1487, #1488)
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Three tickets about the step and merge lifecycle. The decisions on #1486 and #1487 were made by the owner on 2026-10-22 and are recorded on each ticket.

**#1486: a started card goes back to todo only through reset** (option 3).
- `PATCH /api/todos/:id` with `phase: 'todo'` on a started card answers 409 and names `POST /api/todos/:id/reset` (`apps/server/src/routes-todos.ts`). A card counts as started when it is in progress, or when `isStartedTodoRow` finds any build history.
- Why: a PATCH move kept the old builds and the `hasPlan` / `hasChanges` flags. On a GitHub project whose earlier PR had merged, the #1217 guard then treated the next run as a duplicate delivery.
- Still allowed: closed → todo, which is a reopen and keeps history (the detail menu and `reopen_todos`); and a card that never started.
- The web already sends started cards to reset, so nothing changes there.

**#1487: a merge that finishes after its card was cancelled does not land** (option a).
- `finishStep` (`apps/server/src/services/machines.ts`) skips `applyMergeLanding` when the card is closed or in todo. `applyMergeLanding` also checks the card again synchronously right before `updateBranchRef`, so a close during its git checks is caught.
- The hosted repo's default branch stays put. A system row, `MERGE_NOT_LANDED_NOTE`, says the merge did not land.
- A card marked done during the merge still lands, as before.
- `requestMerge` (`apps/server/src/services/builds.ts`) answers 409 when the build already has a merge step pending, waiting for quota or claimed. The check runs first, before any side effect.

**#1488: a step deleted by reset stops on its next heartbeat.**
- The problem: `resetTodo` deleted a claimed step in the same call that signalled its stop, so the daemon's pull of the stop found nothing. The runner swallowed every heartbeat error. The agent ran to the end, spending tokens, holding a slot, and pushing to the old branch.
- Server: `heartbeatStep` answers 410 when the step row no longer exists, and keeps 404 for a step this machine does not hold.
- Daemon: on 410, `runStep` (`apps/daemon/src/runner.ts`) delivers a stop to its own run. The step ends as stopped, which skips commit and push.
- A 404 keeps running. After a release, #1483 lets the same machine's run carry the new claim, and stopping on 404 would break that.
- Mixed server and daemon versions keep the old behaviour.

`/security-review` (`services/machines.ts` is on the list) found no vulnerability.

## Upstream

No new mechanism. The change uses the existing reset route, the step stop slot (`RunStop`, #1495) and HTTP status codes.

## Risk

Two-way door: no schema change, no migration.

What changes for callers:
- A started card PATCHed to todo now gets 409 instead of 200. The web never sends that request for a started card.
- A heartbeat for a missing step gets 410 instead of 404.
- A second merge request while one is in flight gets 409.

- A reset during the few seconds of git after a session ends (the heartbeat has already stopped, per #1473) still commits and pushes. The costly part, the whole agent run, is closed.

- The reset gate lives in the HTTP route only. No other caller moves a card to todo through a manual phase change: chief and MCP `reopen_todos` is closed → todo, which stays allowed.

#1488
- [x] A step claimed by an online daemon is stopped after the card is reset. Server: the heartbeat answers 410 after a reset. Daemon: 410 → `done(stopped)`, no commit or push ([server](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/6a0584afaed0ad63a70be81a74c6defdc9850cd4/docs/verify/1488/new-leg-server.txt), [daemon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/6a0584afaed0ad63a70be81a74c6defdc9850cd4/docs/verify/1488/new-leg-daemon.txt)).

mergedPulls.title: server(1404): merge gate S2 follow-up, compare and checks bound to the PR head
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Follow-up to #1421 (P3 segment S2 of #1404, `docs/spec/28` §4 P3), which was merged at `c4bf400` while pr-gate run 4 at that head said no-go. The blocking finding: the guard `compare.commits.includes(pr.headSha)` also accepts a compare read at a descendant of the PR head, so `mergeReadiness` could report `ready` with a patch digest of a different patch than the PR head's. This PR carries round 9, built on #1421's branch and never pushed there, onto main by cherry-pick ([s2-r9-carry.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/b65f00d46e06419edd20699c0d127b25946633ed/docs/verify/1404/s2-r9-carry.txt)).

- `apps/server/src/services/merge-gate/readiness.ts`, `packages/shared/src/records/merge-gate.ts`: `GateInputs.compare` gains `headSha`, the 40-character SHA the shell put in the compare request's `{head}` slot (the compare response has no head-commit field, checked live; `commits` is chronological and paginated). A compare counts as read at the PR head only when `compare.headSha === pr.headSha` and its `commits` contain `pr.headSha`. Any other compare, older or newer, gives the transient `patch-unavailable` ("compare not read at the PR head") and is treated as unread: no digest, file count, paths, link or verdict judgement, so a race across a push never surfaces as `compare-truncated` (human).
- `GateInputs.checks` gains `headSha`, the SHA the shell read check runs and statuses at. A mismatch gives the transient `required-checks-unreadable` (its label now covers checks not read at the current head) and the checks are treated as unread; under `unstable` the `mergeable-state` blocker says the checks are unreadable.
- A PR that cannot be read still has compare and checks judged, but the result reports neither a head nor a patch digest.
- The shell contract (for S4) is written at the input types: request the compare by SHA, pass a SHA that is not 40 hex characters as `'malformed'`, compare each check run's `head_sha` and the combined status `sha` with `checks.headSha` and pass `null` on a mismatch.
- `packages/shared/test/snapshot.test.ts`: the blocker vocabulary (code, class, label, in order) is frozen in the shared snapshot.

Round 2 (after pr-gate run 1 at `b65f00d`, go with eleven suggestions) binds both reads to the PR head through the response itself, not only the shell's label:

- `compare.commits` entries carry their parents, and `compare.totalCommits` is the response's `total_commits`. `compareHead()` returns the one listed commit that no other listed commit names as a parent; in a complete `base...head` list that is the commit the compare was read at. A compare counts only when its label and its own head both equal the PR head, which catches a read at an older commit, at a descendant, or with a foreign commit mixed in. The list must have exactly `totalCommits` entries and no repeated SHA, otherwise `patch-unavailable` ("compare commit list incomplete").
- Each check run carries its `headSha` and the combined status its `statusSha`; checks count only when every one of them and the requested SHA equal the PR head, otherwise `required-checks-unreadable` and the checks are treated as unread.
- SHAs are checked with `isFullSha` (40 lowercase hex): a malformed PR head gives `pr-unreadable` and no head or digest; a malformed compare SHA gives `compare-malformed` (to a person); a malformed check SHA gives `required-checks-unreadable` with its own detail. Without a usable head the PR's file count and evidence links are not judged against the compare.
- `docs/spec/28` §8: the P3 row now names S1, S2 and S3 as merged and this PR as the S2 follow-up.

Round 3 answers pr-gate run 2 at `1174ebf` (no-go, one blocking finding): `readiness.ts` imported `isFullSha` from `apps/server/src/lib/github.ts`, outside the ADR 0021 D4 ④ gate-source locations, so a PR touching only that file could change which SHAs the gate accepts and be merged as plain product source.

- The SHA check now lives in the gate's own source (`readiness.ts`, compiled once); `lib/github.ts` is unchanged.
- `apps/server/test/merge-gate-imports.test.ts` (new) compiles each gate module with esbuild and reads its imports, so comments cannot hide one: imports only from `@pacman/shared` (and every runtime name taken from it must be the very value `records/merge-gate.ts` exports), `node:crypto` or paths inside `merge-gate/`; no `import()`, `require`, `createRequire`, `import.meta`, `eval`, `Function`, `process` or `globalThis`; no symlink under `merge-gate/`; `records/merge-gate.ts` imports only `zod`.
- Every array and object `records/merge-gate.ts` exports is deep-frozen, so another shared module loaded through the package barrel cannot empty the protected path lists at runtime; `MERGE_BLOCKER_CODES` is typed `readonly`.
- The `pr-unreadable` and `compare-malformed` labels name their new causes; the GateInputs contract says `totalCommits` is page 1's `total_commits` and every page must agree, and that the files are bound to the head because the shell requests every page by the head SHA.

## Verified

Tests first, twice ([s2-r9-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/b65f00d46e06419edd20699c0d127b25946633ed/docs/verify/1404/s2-r9-red-green.txt)), over the four merge-gate test files and the shared snapshot test:

```
red 1   (tests only, source as at c4bf400)   Tests  3 failed | 341 passed (344)
green 1                                      Tests  344 passed (344)
red 2   (tests only, after code-review)      Tests  2 failed | 344 passed (346)
green 2                                      Tests  346 passed (346)
```

Red 1 is the gate's finding: a compare at a descendant with the same file count (and the reverse read), a compare at a descendant with a different count, and checks read at another head. Red 2 comes from the medium /code-review: a compare whose `headSha` matches but whose commits lack the head, and a digest reported for an unreadable PR. Pins green in every leg: an older compare, all three inputs read at a newer commit give `ready`, `unstable` with unreadable or incomplete checks lists both blockers.

Mutations ([s2-mutations-9.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/b65f00d46e06419edd20699c0d127b25946633ed/docs/verify/1404/s2-mutations-9.txt)): 150 applied, 150 caught, none survived (128 from earlier rounds, 22 for round 9: each new rule removed, inverted, classed human, or narrowed to one direction; a digest without a head; the vocabulary reordered).

Gates on the carried head `2edf68e` ([s2-r9-carry.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/b65f00d46e06419edd20699c0d127b25946633ed/docs/verify/1404/s2-r9-carry.txt)): `pnpm lint` (1 existing info in `apps/web`), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, `vitest run --changed origin/main` (2816 passed, 1 skipped) and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0. The round's own gate run on #1421's branch is in [gates-s2-9.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/b65f00d46e06419edd20699c0d127b25946633ed/docs/verify/1404/gates-s2-9.txt). Reviews ([s2-r9-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/b65f00d46e06419edd20699c0d127b25946633ed/docs/verify/1404/s2-r9-reviews.txt)): /code-review at medium on round 9's first fix raised 9 points; 1, 4, 5, 8 and 9 are fixed, 6 is covered by the fix for 1, 2 and 3 are contract notes for S4, and 7 is by design (`block()` keeps one detail per code). /simplify ran as one inline pass; one of its changes, reading blockers straight off the vocabulary, was reverted because the `'human'` fallback for a code outside the vocabulary is deliberate fail-closed code. The run 4 verdict is kept as [pr-gate-1421-run4-c4bf400.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/b65f00d46e06419edd20699c0d127b25946633ed/docs/verify/1404/pr-gate-1421-run4-c4bf400.json).

Round 2, tests first five times ([s2-r10-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/1174ebffd35b2bec7379e4f49f722ae01763a6f0/docs/verify/1404/s2-r10-red-green.txt)): red 3 of 216, 2 of 218, 2 of 220, 1 of 220 and 1 of 221, each green after its fix; the head passes 222 of 222. One simplification (`420c4f9`) was not test-first and let a list padded with a repeated commit through; the next leg put the strict rule back, and the file says so. Mutations ([s2-mutations-10.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/1174ebffd35b2bec7379e4f49f722ae01763a6f0/docs/verify/1404/s2-mutations-10.txt)): 185 applied, 185 caught (140 from earlier rounds, 45 new). GitHub's compare, check-runs and combined-status shapes were captured read-only, including a 399-commit compare paged to its head ([s2-r10-github-shapes.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/1174ebffd35b2bec7379e4f49f722ae01763a6f0/docs/verify/1404/s2-r10-github-shapes.txt)). Gates ([gates-s2-10.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/1174ebffd35b2bec7379e4f49f722ae01763a6f0/docs/verify/1404/gates-s2-10.txt)): lint, typecheck, spec:parse, `vitest run --changed origin/main` (3097 passed, 1 skipped) and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0. Eight /code-review passes at medium, the first on the whole branch against main and each later one on the change pushed after a review ([s2-r10-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/1174ebffd35b2bec7379e4f49f722ae01763a6f0/docs/verify/1404/s2-r10-reviews.txt)); the findings fixed and the ones kept are listed there, and the kept ones are in Risk. The round's gate file at #1421's branch ([gates-s2-9.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/1174ebffd35b2bec7379e4f49f722ae01763a6f0/docs/verify/1404/gates-s2-9.txt)) records `vitest --changed` with exit 1 from the root-only `runner-brief.test.ts` case on a branch without main's newer test; the carried head's run passed.

Gates on `488928c`, with main `9296b8b` merged ([gates-s2-11.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/39a108e80bcd5d82e980599abf32d059b2fbad8c/docs/verify/1404/gates-s2-11.txt)): lint, typecheck, spec:parse, `vitest run --changed origin/main` (3238 passed, 1 skipped) and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0. Five /code-review passes at medium, each on the change since the previous one ([s2-r11-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/39a108e80bcd5d82e980599abf32d059b2fbad8c/docs/verify/1404/s2-r11-reviews.txt)). The verdicts of pr-gate runs 1 and 2 are committed byte for byte ([run 1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/39a108e80bcd5d82e980599abf32d059b2fbad8c/docs/verify/1404/pr-gate-1479-run1-b65f00d.json), [run 2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/39a108e80bcd5d82e980599abf32d059b2fbad8c/docs/verify/1404/pr-gate-1479-run2-1174ebf.json)); that commit alone used the banned-vocabulary exit, for a quoted word in the reviewers' text.

## Upstream

No dependency. GitHub REST compare (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{base}...{head}`): the response carries `base_commit`, `merge_base_commit`, `commits` and `files`, with no field naming the head commit, which is why the shell's requested SHA is the input.

## Risk

Two-way door: `mergeReadiness` is a pure function with no caller on main yet (S4 and S6a wire it), so nothing in production changes. Kept on purpose, both conservative: when the PR is unreadable or its head malformed, the compare and checks are still judged without a head and their blockers listed (round 9's rule, pinned by the `pr-unreadable` true leg); and a deterministic shell fault (malformed PR head or check SHA, a repeated or empty commit list, a non-integer `totalCommits`) is transient, so the gate waits rather than passing, until S4 decides whether these need their own blocker codes (pr-gate run 2 and this round's reviews raised the classification again: a malformed compare SHA already goes to a person, while a malformed PR head or check SHA waits; the conservative direction is kept until S4's shell defines which faults are deterministic). The 40-hex check now exists twice, in the gate and in `lib/github.ts`'s URL builder; if they drift, the gate fails closed. Left from the last review pass, none of which changes what the gate decides: zod schemas in the records module stay mutable, `Date`-like exports are not checked (there are none), and `global` or computed keys could still reach `Function`, which would itself be a gate-source change that needs a human merge. From /code-review, kept with reasons in the reviews file: the duplicated `block()` call (behaviour-neutral; `block()` appends every detail for a code), the single-snapshot architecture, the `isFullSha` import from `lib/github.ts` (no import-time effects), a substitute commit that is a base-side parent of a listed merge (needs the commit graph, which the response does not carry), building the commit set twice, and four low-severity test-wording nits from the last pass. The verdict JSON of #1421's run 4 kept in the evidence contains a negated closing sentence; files are not parsed for keywords. Merge-gate source is ADR 0021 D4 class ④, so this waits for a user merge.

## Acceptance

- [x] A compare or checks read at any commit other than the PR head blocks transiently and is not judged (`merge-gate-readiness.test.ts`, red 1 / green 1)
- [x] Compare commits must contain the head and an unreadable PR reports no digest (red 2 / green 2)
- [x] 150 of 150 mutations caught (`s2-mutations-9.txt`); round 2: 185 of 185 (`s2-mutations-10.txt`)
- [x] Round 2: compare bound by its own head (derived from the parents) and a complete list; checks bound by each run's and the combined status's SHA; malformed SHAs never pass (`s2-r10-red-green.txt`)
- [x] lint / typecheck / spec:parse / vitest --changed / e2e:affected pass on the carried head (`s2-r9-carry.txt`), at round 2 (`gates-s2-10.txt`) and at round 3 (`gates-s2-11.txt`)
- [x] Round 3: gate source imports nothing outside the D4 ④ locations, records data frozen; 200 of 200 mutations caught (`merge-gate-imports.test.ts`, `s2-mutations-11.txt`)

## Issues

```

now carry the SHA they were read at. A compare counts only when that

equal the PR head and its list is complete; checks only when every

other read is a transient blocker and is not judged. Malformed SHAs
never pass. An unreadable PR reports no head or digest. The blocker
vocabulary is frozen in the shared snapshot; spec 28's P3 row is
brought up to date. The gate keeps its SHA check in its own source,
a test holds gate modules to imports from the D4 gate-source
```

mergedPulls.body:
## What

P5 follow-up for #1406 (bootstrap phase P5a). It carries two sets of work that landed after their PRs merged:

- **#1461 round 5** (the issue intake poller, merged at `0471b6b` while round 5 was still being built), from pr-gate run 4 on #1461;
- **#1477 round 2** (the webhook `pacman` trigger under D5 and the cap, #1459, merged at `1573cda`), from pr-gate run 1 on #1477, which returned no-go after the merge ([comment](https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/pull/1477#issuecomment-6320494787)).

Both touch the intake files and spec 28 §4 P5a, so they share one PR.

**Webhook** (`apps/server/src/services/webhook.ts`, `packages/shared/src/webhook.ts`):
- Owner and repo come from `githubRepoOfProject(repoRow)` instead of splitting `full_name`. A stored `githubRepo` with a `.` or `..` segment answers 202 `misconfigured` (`malformed-repo`) and sends nothing. Before, the permission read sent the team token to a rewritten path, the #1466 class.
- A sender login that does not have a GitHub login's shape (`..`, `.`, `a/b`) is refused as `sender-malformed` before any request. A `[bot]` login is still accepted.
- The three sender refusals (below triage, permission unreadable, rate limited) answer one generic 202 sentence. The reason code and the specific detail (login, repo, reset time) go to the log line only, so the URL-token holder no longer reads a login's permission verdict from the answer. This narrows that leak; the Risk section says what is left.
- The 'github webhook import accepted' audit line is written before orchestration, so it survives an orchestration error.
- The import's own 404 is told apart by reading the team token again: a missing connection, or an issue not found on GitHub (`issue-not-found`).

**Rate limits** (`apps/server/src/lib/github.ts`):
- `retry-after` is preferred over `x-ratelimit-reset`, as GitHub's rate-limit docs say.
- Both headers count only as non-negative integers, so an empty `retry-after` is no longer 0 seconds.

**Intake** (`apps/server/src/services/issue-intake.ts`, comments only):
- Tests for a later events page that cannot be read, malformed events voiding the whole read, the closer check on a malformed `closed` event, and an import's rate limit failing only that import.
- The six negative-only intake tests now assert the candidate was evaluated.

**Probe** (`.claude/skills/verify-pacman/scripts/drive-1137-webhook-tracer.mjs`, `vp-registry.json`):
- The registered webhook probe sends `sender: { login: VERIFY_GITHUB_SENDER }`. The variable defaults to the repo's owner segment, which suits a user-owned repository.
- It checks the refusals (no sender, a ghost sender, at cap, nothing imported) and their reason codes in `server.log`. The case's purpose and failure list name them.

**Docs:**
- spec 28 §4 P5a states the D5 conditions the code checks, the webhook rule, and the rate-limit rule. It also says what the GitHub App check does and does not catch.
- spec 28 §8 updates only the P5 row.
- Both READMEs say the same.

## Verified

- Each new rule turns a test red when undone, and the six negative-only tests fail under a no-op sweep; mutations in [p5a1-r5-mutations.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e1a6ad1576a679d86db5bade0ba78e94dda65b5a/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-r5-mutations.json) with the driver [p5a1-r5-mutate.mjs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e1a6ad1576a679d86db5bade0ba78e94dda65b5a/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-r5-mutate.mjs).
- Gates at `0567408` ([gates-p5a1-r5.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e1a6ad1576a679d86db5bade0ba78e94dda65b5a/docs/verify/1406/gates-p5a1-r5.txt)) exit 0.
- Reviews: [p5a1-r5-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e1a6ad1576a679d86db5bade0ba78e94dda65b5a/docs/verify/1406/p5a1-r5-reviews.txt).

#1459 round 2, tests before fixes twice ([r2-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e1a6ad1576a679d86db5bade0ba78e94dda65b5a/docs/verify/1459/r2-red-green.txt)):

```
red   45b87f1 (tests only)                 19 of 212 fail
green bfa8b01                              241 passed (webhook, issue-intake, github-issues)
red   022c6a1 (review tests only)          8 of 252 fail
green b9f6d92                              436 passed (six files)
```

Mutations, ten in all, each undoing one rule ([r2-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e1a6ad1576a679d86db5bade0ba78e94dda65b5a/docs/verify/1459/r2-mutations.txt)):

- **Intake and rate limits:** the in-flight count in the poller, `retry-after` first, integer-only headers.

Every mutation turns a test red.

Gates at `43e47e3`, with main `50a5500` merged ([gates-r2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e1a6ad1576a679d86db5bade0ba78e94dda65b5a/docs/verify/1459/gates-r2.txt)): exit 0 for

- `pnpm typecheck`;
- `pnpm spec:parse`;
- `vitest run --changed origin/main` (3173 passed, 1 skipped);
- `e2e:affected` (8 passed);
- the verify-pacman self-test (66 of 66) and registry gate.

The gate run I made at #1477's merge head is kept as [gates-1573cda.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e1a6ad1576a679d86db5bade0ba78e94dda65b5a/docs/verify/1459/gates-1573cda.txt). Dated notes appended to [failure-modes.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e1a6ad1576a679d86db5bade0ba78e94dda65b5a/docs/verify/1459/failure-modes.txt) record that 429 now has its own reason and add rows F16 to F22.

The registered probe was not run live: this session has no GitHub token a local stack can use. It was checked with `node --check` and a `--force --dry-run`.

Reviews ([r2-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e1a6ad1576a679d86db5bade0ba78e94dda65b5a/docs/verify/1459/r2-reviews.txt)): /code-review at medium. /security-review is not required, since neither `routes-webhook.ts` nor any other AGENTS.md-listed file is touched. The skill was still tried twice, but it read another checkout both times, so the security-relevant files were reviewed by hand under its rules. No finding reached confidence 8.

## Upstream

No dependency. GitHub REST: the collaborator permission read and the rate-limit headers, quoted with URLs in the evidence files.

## Risk

Two-way door. Kept from /code-review, with reasons in the reviews files:
- The URL-token holder can still tell some outcomes apart after the permission check. Closing that needs uniform answers after the check.
- The logged reset time is computed from when the sweep started (log only).
- An import whose orchestration fails (no chief bound) stays in to-do holding a cap slot. A chief-binding check before the import would avoid it.
- The duplicate check runs after the permission read.
- No webhook test sends both rate-limit headers.

Design questions and security-sensitive paths stay as follow-ups on #1406 ([comment](https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1406#issuecomment-6320594539)):
- a refused label is final;
- the webhook does not refuse an app-applied label;
- the connection token reaches hook environments;
- review tasks without a PR are not closed with their issue;
- the close check accepts an app close.

The patch touches `.claude/skills/`, `README*` and `docs/spec/28`, so it waits for a user merge.

## Acceptance

mergedPulls.title: server(1403): the reconcile follows the build's own PR; review-gate wake text and confirm check
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment 2 of #1403 (bootstrap phase P2, `docs/spec/28` §4 P2), on top of segment 1 (#1414, merged as `b616110`). The plan and its decisions are on #1403; the API merge the user decided on 2026-10-22 (design D) is segment 2b, built next on top of this branch.

- **The build's PR identity** (`apps/server/src/services/ci-loop.ts`, `apps/server/src/lib/github.ts`). Before a confirmed close fails the card, the sweep lists the PRs of the build's conversation branch into the default base (`pulls?state=all&head=<owner>:<branch>&base=<default>`, owner taken from the PR response's `base.repo.owner.login`, so a renamed or transferred repository still matches). When one of them is the build's own (same repository by id, its own branch), it is recorded on the build instead of failing the card: an open PR wins, otherwise the newest merged one, and only if it is newer than the build's newest PR closed without merge. The build's PR number is replaced only if the daemon has not changed it meanwhile (compare-and-set), and the adoption row is written once per round. If the recorded PR shows up open or merged in the list, that counts as a reopen or a merge: nothing is written and the card is read again. Two failed list reads in a row fall back to segment 1 (the card fails as before). A recorded PR that is not the build's own gets the same lookup every 10 minutes (hourly without a GitHub connection), with segment 1's hint as the fallback. Before this, a person who closed PR #N and opened #M from the same branch saw the card fail while #M was open.
- **G9** (`apps/server/src/services/chief.ts`, `apps/server/src/services/builds.ts`). The review gate has its own wake text: do not call `confirm_builds` or `merge_builds`, report readiness, point to the 完成 button. Before, the review gate reused the confirm gate's text, and a chief that followed it wrote a "通过了确认" row before the confirm was refused with 409. A confirm is now accepted only in the confirm phase, checked before the announcement row is written; this also refuses a second confirm in building and a confirm on a queued direct-execution task, both of which used to queue a duplicate build step (409 now; the user chose to keep this on 2026-10-22).
- **Test pins** that segment 1 left without a test (each shown by a surviving mutation in pr-gate runs 10 and 11 on #1414): a closed outcome reported once per round across a second sweep 600 s after the reopen (⑱d, ⑱f), `roundStart` counting only build and plan steps, `closedSeenAt` cleared when the card leaves review, a failed build step's pushed checkpoint not deciding containment, the stopped-step filters, and ⑧b sweeping twice so the closed half of "an older build's PR does not decide the current build" has its own pin.
- `docs/spec/02` §4.2 describes the adoption; `docs/spec/28` §8 updates only the P2 row.

## Verified

Failure modes first ([seg2-failure-modes.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e92277d2b209ce9ea3f4b6b162c5975b9e72982b/docs/verify/1403/seg2-failure-modes.txt)); the branch PR list was captured live from this repository and the captures are the test fixtures ([seg2-live-capture.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e92277d2b209ce9ea3f4b6b162c5975b9e72982b/docs/verify/1403/seg2-live-capture.txt)). Tests before code ([seg2-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e92277d2b209ce9ea3f4b6b162c5975b9e72982b/docs/verify/1403/seg2-red-green.txt)):

```
first leg (tests of cf1bca1, sources of cefad17)   Tests  22 failed | 158 passed (180)  ->  180 passed
final leg (tests of 034441e, sources of main)      Tests  40 failed | 157 passed (197)  ->  197 passed
```

The whole server project passed (122 files, 1844 tests) on the tree that became `3f37f34`. Mutations ([seg2-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e92277d2b209ce9ea3f4b6b162c5975b9e72982b/docs/verify/1403/seg2-mutations.txt)): 47 run on the final sources, 46 caught, and one (M06) is equivalent, because its rule is already implied by the newer-than-rejected filter; the file explains it. A control run shows ⑧b with one sweep lets the "no current-build rule" mutation through and with two sweeps catches it.

Gates at `9be7206`, with origin/main `659d8cb` merged ([gates-seg2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e92277d2b209ce9ea3f4b6b162c5975b9e72982b/docs/verify/1403/gates-seg2.txt)): `pnpm lint` (1 existing info in `apps/web`), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, `vitest run --changed origin/main` (139 files, 1643 passed) and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0. Reviews ([seg2-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e92277d2b209ce9ea3f4b6b162c5975b9e72982b/docs/verify/1403/seg2-reviews.txt)): /simplify as one inline pass (two cleanups), /code-review at medium four times (9, 9, 9 and 4 findings), most fixed and the rest kept there with reasons. /security-review is not required: no file on the AGENTS.md list is touched and the only new GitHub call is a read.

## Upstream

No dependency. GitHub REST `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls` with `state=all`, `head=user:ref-name` and `base`, as documented at https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls#list-pull-requests (quoted in the plan on #1403 and in the failure-modes file).

## Risk

Two-way door. The confirm phase check changes the API in two cases from a silent duplicate build step to 409; the user chose to keep it. The daemon's PR probe (`apps/daemon/src/github-probe.ts`) still records the highest-numbered open PR by branch name, without owner or base, so a same-named fork PR or a backport PR can be recorded and re-recorded after an adoption; that is the root cause of two kept review findings and goes to a follow-up. The fourth /code-review pass's fixes are covered by their own tests and the mutation run rather than a fifth review. /simplify ran inline, not as the four-agent fan-out. The patch touches `docs/spec/02` and `docs/spec/28` and is 2,567 lines, so it waits for a user merge.

## Acceptance

- [x] A closed PR whose branch has the build's own open or newer merged PR adopts it instead of failing the card; a foreign recorded PR is looked up and adopted (`pr-reconcile.test.ts`, red/green)
- [x] The review gate's wake text no longer asks for a confirm, and a confirm outside the confirm phase is refused before any row is written (`chief-watch.test.ts`, `chief-auto-confirm.test.ts`, `gate-actor.test.ts`)
- [x] The test pins listed on #1403 for segment 2, plus ⑧b sweeping twice (`seg2-mutations.txt`)
- [x] 46 of 47 mutations caught, the remaining one equivalent (`seg2-mutations.txt`)
- [x] lint / typecheck / spec:parse / vitest --changed / e2e:affected pass (`gates-seg2.txt`)

## Issues

Part of #1403 (segment 2). Segment 3 carries the closing line for #1403; this squash body has none. The PR's commit list also shows segment 1's commits from before its squash, because main holds #1414 only as a squash; the content diff is segment 2 only.

Squash with this message:

```

Before a confirmed close fails the card, the sweep lists the PRs of
the build's branch into the default base and adopts the build's own
open, or newer merged, PR instead (compare-and-set on the build's PR
number, one row per round); a recorded PR that is not the build's own
gets the same lookup on a timer. The review gate gets its own chief
wake text, and a confirm is accepted only in the confirm phase, checked
before the announcement row. Test pins for segment 1's surviving
```

mergedPulls.body:
## What

Follow-up to #1475 (P5 segment 3 of #1406: GitHub issue text fenced as data), which was merged while its pr-gate run 1 at `7f5d250` was still running; that run returned no-go with two blocking findings, each confirmed by two skeptics ([comment on #1475](https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/pull/1475#issuecomment-6318578603)). This PR fixes both and four cheap suggestions from the same run.

- **Images inside the fence are delivered again** (`apps/daemon/src/step-attachments.ts`, `packages/shared/src/records/prompts.ts`). #1475 quotes every line of an issue-sourced task's text with `> `, so an attachment token line a team member later adds to the spec (chief or MCP `update_todo`, REST PATCH) reached the daemon as a quoted line (`> ` followed by the image token); `resolveStepImages` only accepts whole token lines, so the image was neither delivered nor noted as undelivered, on plan, build and verify steps. `resolveStepImages` now also accepts a line that is the fence's quote prefix plus a whole token line, but only inside a fence: the shared `issueFenceQuotedLines` opens the fence only on the bare head line and closes it only on the bare closing line, which issue text cannot produce because every line of it is quoted. The anchor, the materialized-path note and both "not delivered" notes go back through the shared `quoteIssueLines` (also used by `fenceIssueText`), so every resulting line stays quoted, also when a file name or error text carries `\r`, U+2028 or U+0085; alt text never leaves its quoted line. Quoted tokens outside a fence and doubly quoted tokens are untouched, and `ATTACHMENT_TOKEN_LINE` is unchanged for its other users. `safeFileName` also drops U+0085, U+2028, U+2029 and format characters, so the path the agent is told to read matches the file on disk.
- **Issue titles reach chief wake prompts only inside the fence** (`apps/server/src/services/chief.ts`). For an issue-sourced task, `wakeFacts` names it as `#n（标题出自 GitHub issue，原文在下方围栏里）` and appends `fenceIssueText(sourceRef, title)`; other tasks keep their wake text byte for byte (the switch moved unchanged into `wakeFactText`). The chief system rule now names orchestrate requests and wake prompts. The wake row in the chief thread shows the fence for issue tasks.
- **Cheap suggestions:** format characters (Unicode Cf: bidi overrides, zero-width, tag characters) are removed from fenced issue text, plain tasks keep theirs; the one-line `quotesIssueFence` is inlined at its single call site (`chief-tools.ts`); `docs/spec/02` §4.4 states the `save_memory` refusal of fenced text; the merge, ci-fix and degraded fresh-session prompt variants get direct tests.

## Verified

Failure modes first ([p5-3-fix-failure-modes.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/ff385a44c96b6090fc06525dfc5516f30ad34edf/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-fix-failure-modes.txt)), then the failing tests on unchanged sources ([p5-3-fix-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/ff385a44c96b6090fc06525dfc5516f30ad34edf/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-fix-red-green.txt)), over the shared, daemon and server fence tests:

The new server tests drive `triggerChiefWakes` through confirm, review, failed and done, a split parent and hostile titles, and assert the title appears only on quoted lines inside the fence; plain, orchestration and self-issue tasks are pinned. Reviews in [p5-3-fix-reviews-2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/ebfe743b28527dc62f080649531501e7ad694c18/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-fix-reviews-2.txt). pr-gate run 2 at `ebfe743` said go with no blocking finding and seven suggestions: the squash message above now carries round 2's behaviour, and the rest are in Risk. One asked for the tests to run on the tree merged with today's main (#1483 changes `apps/daemon/src/runner.ts`): on a temporary merge of `659d8cb` into this head, not committed, the shared, daemon and server fence tests plus `step-reclaim.test.ts` pass 73 of 73 (5 files); the merge was textually clean and was undone, so the head stays the one pr-gate reviewed.

A daemon older than this fix still drops images on the verify step of an issue-sourced task, because the server has fenced the verify instruction since #1475; that needs the daemon upgrade and cannot be undone on the server without unfencing those lines. On plan and build the daemon builds the text, so a pre-#1475 daemon delivers images unfenced and this fix delivers them fenced. Kept from /code-review, with reasons in the reviews file: a token in the issue body itself triggers a team-scoped download again, as before #1475. The ids are random but not secret: a self-created issue posts a task's spec, token lines included, to GitHub, so an outside author can copy one into a new issue; the agent's `attachment` tool could already fetch any team attachment by id, so this removes a model step rather than adding a capability. mergedPulls.title: server(1459): webhook pacman trigger follows D5 and the in-flight cap
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Ticket #1459, as decided by the user on 2026-10-21 (https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1459#issuecomment-6316379513): the webhook's `pacman` label trigger stays, follows ADR 0021 D5, and counts against the per-project in-flight cap. Stacked on #1461 (the issue intake poller), whose permission read and cap it reuses; the base moves to main after #1461 merges.

- `apps/server/src/services/webhook.ts`: on `issues` + `labeled` + `pacman`, the event's `sender` (the user who applied the label) must have triage, write, maintain or admin on the repository. The checks run in this order: sender present, cap (database only), team token, sender's permission, cap again just before the import. A label applied by an outside author, a read-only user or the `ghost` placeholder is not imported. A permission read that fails (403, 5xx, network, timeout, malformed) imports nothing and is not cached. A rate-limited read (429, or 403 with GitHub's rate-limit headers or its secondary-limit message) does the same and answers with its own reason code, plus the reset time when GitHub gives one. The webhook answers 202 with a reason in every refused case, so GitHub does not redeliver, and logs `github webhook import refused` with the delivery id, project, repo, issue, sender and a reason code (`sender-below-triage`, `permission-unreadable`, `rate-limited`, `no-github-connection`, `token-unreadable`, `at-cap`, `no-sender`). A stored token that does not decrypt answers `misconfigured` instead of a 500. A webhook import keeps the seed user as its creator, so the poller's close reconcile does not act on it.
- `apps/server/src/services/issue-intake.ts` exports the poller's team token read, in-flight count and permission read with its cache (`teamGithubToken`, `projectAtInFlightCap`, `hasRepoTriage`), so the webhook and the poller share one cache whether or not `PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE` is on.
- `apps/server/src/services/github-issues.ts` records which project each import in flight belongs to, and the cap counts those too: labeling several issues at once sends one event per issue, and two events arriving together both passed a count of stored tasks alone. The poller's count gains the same.
- `packages/shared/src/webhook.ts`: `sender` is an optional field of the payload schema.
- `README.md` and `README.zh.md`: the `PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE` row states the webhook rule.

## Verified

GitHub's docs on `sender` and the `ghost` user are quoted with URLs in [api-notes.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/29e16537e6d1e2d537d2bc9b79ad2cf123251a79/docs/verify/1459/api-notes.txt). They do not say who the sender is for a label an issue template adds; the closest evidence is that labels set at creation show as `labeled` events by the issue's creator. The rule fails closed either way. Failure modes first ([failure-modes.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/29e16537e6d1e2d537d2bc9b79ad2cf123251a79/docs/verify/1459/failure-modes.txt)).

The new tests on `f8f56f4` (tests only, sources as `69722cc`) fail 22 of 163; at `3524b15` 163 of 163 pass ([red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/29e16537e6d1e2d537d2bc9b79ad2cf123251a79/docs/verify/1459/red-green.txt)). Three new tests pass on both sides as guards (an unrelated label, a wrong token, a redelivery). 20 mutations each turn a test red ([mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/29e16537e6d1e2d537d2bc9b79ad2cf123251a79/docs/verify/1459/mutations.txt)): the D5 check dropped, an unreadable permission treated as allowed, either cap check dropped, imports in flight not counted, the cache off, a cache only for the webhook, failures cached, a read without a token, the cipher error escaping, a missing sender allowed, no log line, 403 instead of 202, another creator, two role-rule changes, the poller's count and the label filter.

Live, this branch's server on port 8796 with a scratch home ([live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/29e16537e6d1e2d537d2bc9b79ad2cf123251a79/docs/verify/1459/live.txt)): a wrong token gives 401; another label, no sender, no connection, a token that does not decrypt, a project at the cap and a redelivery each give the answer above, and nothing is imported (the database holds only the 3 seeded tasks). The server has no GitHub base-URL override, so the qualifying-permission path is shown by tests; the permission read itself ran against GitHub, which answered 401 to the dummy token, and the import was refused as `permission-unreadable`.

Gates ([gates.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/29e16537e6d1e2d537d2bc9b79ad2cf123251a79/docs/verify/1459/gates.txt)): `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, the spawn gate and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` passes 2641 with the one root-only failure (`runner-brief.test.ts` "擦除失败"). `/code-review` at low effort on `69722cc..HEAD` raised one point, a detail text for a missing secret box that the webhook path cannot reach; kept, with the reason, in [reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/29e16537e6d1e2d537d2bc9b79ad2cf123251a79/docs/verify/1459/reviews.txt). This diff does not touch `routes-webhook.ts`; a security pass on it found nothing at the skill's threshold ([security-review.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/29e16537e6d1e2d537d2bc9b79ad2cf123251a79/docs/verify/1459/security-review.txt)).

Round 2 merges #1461 round 4 (`22cf8db`) into this branch with a merge commit (`a7e9707`); the four conflicts and how each was resolved are in [merge-p5-r4.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/cd48837a4294645c19dc82608bef27035b38df2e/docs/verify/1459/merge-p5-r4.txt). Round 4's permission read now throws its rate-limit error, which the webhook answered with a 500, and round 4's new tests sent no `sender`, which this branch refuses: 3 of 214 failed at the merge. The tests were committed first (`2d0a4a2`, 4 failed), then the fix (`7060191`): the webhook answers a rate-limited permission read with 202 `rate-limited` and does not cache it (test W4b: 429 with and without `retry-after`, 403 with the rate-limit headers, 403 with only the secondary-limit message). Gates at `7060191` ([gates-2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/cd48837a4294645c19dc82608bef27035b38df2e/docs/verify/1459/gates-2.txt)): lint, typecheck, spec:parse, the spawn gate, `vitest run --changed origin/main` (2847 passed, 1 skipped) and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0.

## Upstream

No dependency. The permission read is `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{username}/permission` (`role_name`), as #1461 uses it.

## Risk

Two-way door. The `pacman` trigger now needs a labeler with triage or above and a GitHub connection on the team; a team without a connection, or a labeler below triage, gets no import where it used to. The webhook payload is authenticated only by the URL token, so a holder of that token can name any `sender`; this is stricter than before, when a token holder could import any issue with no check. The rule for a template-applied label rests on the sender being the issue's author, which GitHub's docs do not state; if GitHub ever reported a maintainer there, an outside author's issue would be imported, as it is today.

The poller (#1461 round 4) refuses a `ready-for-agent` label applied through a GitHub App; the webhook checks only the event's `sender` and reads no app field, so a `pacman` label applied by an app acting for a user with triage or above still imports. Applying the same refusal on the webhook needs the issue's events read the poller makes; it is kept as a follow-up for a later P5 segment rather than widened here.

The patch is 1,843 lines (868 outside `docs/verify/`) across 18 files against #1461's branch and edits the READMEs, outside the ADR 0021 D4 auto-merge set, so it waits for a user merge.

## Acceptance

- [x] An outside author's label (issue template) is not imported; triage and above are (`webhook.test.ts`, `red-green.txt`)
- [x] A failed permission read imports nothing and is logged (`webhook.test.ts`, `live.txt`)
- [x] Webhook and poller importing one issue at once give one task; the cap counts imports in flight (`webhook.test.ts`, `mutations.txt`)
- [x] lint / typecheck / spec:parse / vitest --changed / e2e:affected pass, except the root-only runner-brief case (`gates.txt`)
- [x] #1461 round 4 merged in; a rate-limited permission read answers 202 `rate-limited` and is not cached; gates pass again (`merge-p5-r4.txt`, `gates-2.txt`)

## Issues

Builds on #1461. The squash message below carries the closing line for #1459.

Squash with this message:

```
server(1459): webhook pacman trigger follows D5 and the in-flight cap (#1477)

The webhook's issues/labeled/pacman trigger imports only when the
event's sender has triage or above on the repository, read with the
issue poller's permission read and cache, and only while the project
is under the per-project in-flight cap, which now also counts imports
still waiting on GitHub. A refused event answers 202 with a reason and
is logged; a failed permission read imports nothing. A token that does
not decrypt answers misconfigured instead of 500, and a rate-limited
permission read answers 202 rate-limited.

closes #1459
```

mergedPulls.title: server(1406): issue intake poller for ready-for-agent issues, opt-in
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment 1 of 3 for #1406 (bootstrap phase P5a, `docs/spec/28` on #1410): the server takes `ready-for-agent` issues from GitHub on its own, under ADR 0021 D5. The plan and the failure modes are in the ticket comment (https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1406#issuecomment-6311590280).

- `apps/server/src/services/issue-intake.ts` is a new loop in the scheduler family, every 5 minutes, beside the CI grind's timer (`scheduler.ts`); `tick()` stays free of network reads. It is off unless `PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE` is `1`, `true` or `yes` (`config.ts`, `packages/shared/src/brand.ts`), and the server logs at startup whether it is on. Per team with a GitHub token (no anonymous reads) and per project whose `githubRepo` is a well-formed `owner/repo`:
  - The project is skipped before any import when the team's chief is not bound to an agent with a model (`chiefBinding` in `chief.ts`, the same chief row and check `sendChiefMessage` uses), so no card is created that `orchestrateTodo` would refuse.
  - A conditional list read of open issues labeled `ready-for-agent`, oldest first (`sort=created&direction=asc`, 100 per page, following `rel="next"` for up to 3 pages; a 304 reuses the cached list). Pull requests in the list are skipped.
  - In-flight cap: at most 3 `github-issue` tasks per project outside done and closed (failed counts); only the remaining room is imported, oldest first, and the list is not read when the project is full.
  - D5 per candidate: the issue's events are read, the newest `labeled` event for `ready-for-agent` decides, and its actor must be a person (a label applied through a GitHub App, `performed_via_github_app` set, is not taken and is logged with the app's slug) with triage, write, maintain or admin on the repository (`collaborators/{login}/permission`, read through `role_name`, cached 15 minutes). The events read follows up to 5 pages; a later `unlabeled`, a history longer than that, a malformed event, or any failed read means the issue is not taken this sweep. A 429, or a 403 with rate-limit signals, on any intake read stops that team's sweep for the run and logs the reset time.
  - Import through `importGithubIssue` (409 when the issue already has a task, team-wide) with `createdBy` set to the team chief's bound agent id, which marks the task as the poller's (the REST import and the webhook keep the seed user), then `orchestrateTodo`. A failed orchestrate is retried on later sweeps, at most 3 attempts in all, and stops when the task has left todo, a person has started it, or the chief is now bound to another agent; the count is kept in memory.
  - An issue closed on GitHub closes a task the poller imported (its `createdBy` is the team chief's current bound agent) through `transitionTodos(..., 'closed')`, the close funnel that stops the task's active steps (#1445, #1451), but only when this process saw the issue open first (at import or in an earlier read) and the newest `closed` event's actor has triage or above. A task imported by hand from an issue that was already closed, or any issue first seen closed after a restart, is never closed by the poller, and a reopened task stays open. A task in review, or any task with a build that delivered a PR, is left to the PR reconcile of #1414, so a merge that closes the issue ends in done rather than closed. While the chief is unbound nothing is reconciled for that team, and what the poller saw open is kept until it is bound again. The phase is read again right before the write.
  - The sweep never overlaps itself, logs one tally line (`issue intake sweep`), and logs `issue intake sweep failed` with the reason when something outside the per-team handling throws.
- `apps/server/src/services/github-issues.ts`: `importGithubIssue` takes an in-process claim on team and sourceRef before its GitHub reads and releases it in `finally`, so the webhook and the poller importing the same issue at once give one task and one 409. `todo.sourceRef` has no unique index; the claim covers one server process.
- `apps/server/src/lib/github.ts`: four reads in the issue section after `githubRepoLabels` (`githubOpenIssuesWithLabel`, `githubIssueEvents`, `githubCollaboratorPermission`, `githubIssueState`); the events read keeps `performed_via_github_app` as `viaApp`, and the "issue intake candidate taken" log line names the labeler and `viaApp` with a local conditional GET. They sit outside the regions #1414 rewrites; `git merge-tree` against #1414, #1420 and #1421 shows no conflict.

## Upstream

No dependency polls GitHub issues here. The rules come from the GitHub REST docs, quoted with URLs in `api-notes.txt`: the issues list returns pull requests marked by `pull_request`; issue events carry `labeled` and `unlabeled` with `actor.login`, `label.name` and `created_at`, paged with a `Link` header; `collaborators/{username}/permission` answers 200 or 404 and needs only Metadata read, and its `permission` field maps maintain to write and triage to read, so the intake reads `role_name`; a 304 to an authorized conditional request does not count against the primary rate limit. Events were chosen over the timeline API because the timeline also returns comment bodies.

## Risk

Two-way door, and off by default: nothing changes until `PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE` is set. Once it is set, a team with a GitHub connection and a bound chief gets its oldest labeled issues imported and dispatched, up to 3 open per project; this repository labels most issues `ready-for-agent` for the issue-label gate, so the README says to check the labels first. Spec 28 P8 is where it would be turned on for real (drill repository first).

Left as they are, with the reason:
- The claim against double import holds within one server process; a unique index on `todo(teamId, sourceRef)` would cover several instances but needs a migration, which belongs with the migration-numbering rules at merge time.
- A failed orchestrate is retried at most 3 times; the count lives in memory, so a restart forgets a task that still waits, which a person then starts.
- The poller's tasks show the chief's agent as their creator. Rebinding the chief to another agent leaves the tasks taken under the old one outside the close reconcile.
- The per-project cap of 3 counts every open `github-issue` task, including ones imported by hand or by the webhook, which the reconcile does not close; they hold slots until a person closes them. The cap limits work in flight per project whatever its source.
- A closed task keeps its sourceRef, so an issue reopened and labeled again is not imported again (409).
- An issue with more than 500 events is never taken, and only the 300 oldest labeled issues are read each sweep (`listTruncated` counts a cut); a deleted or transferred issue (404, 410) leaves its task as it is.
- The close reconcile only acts on changes this process saw, so an issue closed while the server was down leaves its task open until a person closes it.
- D5 vets who applied the label, not the text: an issue body or title edited after labeling is imported as it stands, as data (spec 28: the merge gate and D4 are the guard). A label applied through a GitHub App is not taken, so an agent session holding the owner's authorization cannot feed the intake its own issues; a person relabels such an issue to have it taken.
- A task in review, or with a delivered PR, is left to #1414's PR reconcile, which is not on main yet; until it is, such a task stays as it is when its issue closes.
- No end-to-end run against GitHub with a real team token: the proxy refuses the permission endpoint, so the import path is shown by tests over captured shapes and the live run above shows the switch. The run on a long-lived instance with a drill repository is a host leg (spec 28 §8, 待宿主).
- `intakeGet` in `lib/github.ts` is a second conditional GET beside #1414's `conditionalGetJson`; they merge into one after #1414 lands, to keep the two PRs free of conflicts now.
- The webhook trigger follows D5 in #1477 (#1459), stacked on this PR.
- The close reconcile's two correlated NOT EXISTS checks (delivered PR, open children) have no index; they run once per sweep, every 5 minutes.
- A 429 on an import's own detail or labels read counts as that import's failure; the next candidate's events read then stops the team.
- Code-review findings left as they are, each with its reason, are listed in `p5a1-r4-reviews.txt`.

The patch is 9,626 lines (5,015 outside `docs/verify/`) across 58 files, over ADR 0021 D4's 800-line cap, and edits `docs/spec/28` and the READMEs outside the auto-merge set, so it waits for a user merge.

## Acceptance

- [x] Intake filter unit tests: label, labeler permission, newest event, already imported, in-flight cap (`issue-intake.test.ts`, groups 1 to 14)
- [x] Webhook and poller importing the same issue at once give one task (`github-issues.test.ts`, `webhook.test.ts`, `issue-intake.test.ts`)
- [x] Close reconcile: only an observed open-to-closed change by a closer with triage or above closes a task; a task imported from a closed issue, or reopened, stays open (round 2, `p5a1-r2-red-green.txt`); only the poller's tasks, never one with a delivered PR (round 3, `p5a1-r3-red-green.txt`, `p5a1-r3b-red-green.txt`)
- [x] A failed orchestrate after the import is retried, bounded (round 3, `p5a1-r3-red-green.txt`)
- [x] Split parents, ref case, rate limits and app-applied labels handled (round 4, `p5a1-r4-red-green.txt`)
- [x] Off by default; on with `PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE`; the server says which at startup (`p5a1-optin-*.txt`)
- [x] Mutations: each of 13 rules in round 1, 30 in round 2 and 29 in round 3 and 15 in round 4 turns a test red when undone (`p5a1-mutations.txt`, `p5a1-r2-mutations.txt`, `p5a1-r3-mutations.txt`, `p5a1-r3b-mutations.txt`, `p5a1-r4-mutations.txt`)
- [x] lint / typecheck / spec:parse / vitest --changed / e2e:affected pass, except the root-only runner-brief case (`gates-p5a1.txt` to `gates-p5a1-6.txt`)

mergedPulls.title: server(1403): reconcile review-phase PRs merged or closed on GitHub
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment 1 of 3 for #1403 (bootstrap phase P2, `docs/spec/28` on #1410): a todo in review learns what happened to its PR on GitHub.

Today a GitHub-form todo stays in review after its PR is merged on GitHub, because nothing reads the PR once the CI grind (`apps/server/src/services/ci-loop.ts`, building phase only) hands it over. A PR closed without merging leaves the card in review as well.

- `ci-loop.ts` gets a second candidate set in the same 60 s sweep: builds that have a PR number, whose todo is in `review`, that are the todo's current build (`todo.latestBuildId`), and that have no step in flight (claimed, or queued or waiting for quota other than a verify or review step). An older build's PR never decides a newer build's fate, a merge step that is merging the PR finishes the todo itself, and an offline or quota-blocked Verifier does not pin the card. The checks run again after each network read. Each candidate gets one conditional GET of `pulls/{n}`; a PR already read as merged is not read again, since a merge is final, unless that response lacked the base or head fields the merge check needs (it is then read again under the same throttles). Without a GitHub connection a PR is read at most every five minutes, the reconcile spends at most 20 anonymous requests an hour of its own and stops when it and the grind together reach 50 (GitHub allows 60 per IP; the rest is left to the #931 / #1217 guards), a pulls read starts only with room left for the compare it may need, and the PR read longest ago goes first.
  - Merged into the default branch, by anyone: a system row `PR #n 已在 GitHub 合并（合并提交 abc1234，由 <login> 合并）`, then `finishTodoDone`. When the build's last pushed checkpoint (any step but review, ordered by when the step last checked in) is not contained in the merged head (`compare/{checkpoint}...{head}?per_page=1` is not ahead or identical, or the commit is unknown to GitHub), the merge missed later work: one hint names the commit and the card stays in review. A merge into, or a close of, a PR with another base, or a response without a head sha or base, leaves the card in review (with one hint for another base).
  - Closed without merge into the default branch, and still closed at the next read 50 s or more later (closing and reopening a PR to rerun CI is common; an open read, a skipped or failed read resets the count, and the time is when each read happened, not when the sweep started): a closed row, `build.errorMessage` (a person most likely decided against the change; restart opens a new branch, spec 23 R3), and `failed`.
  - Each outcome is reported once per round. A round starts at the build's latest build or plan step, so a #931 rework round on the same build starts fresh. The markers are this round's completion row (written by the merge step or the reconcile) and the reconcile's own closed row. A person who moves the card back into review after the report keeps it there; a finish by hand before the reconcile saw the outcome is followed by one report. No clock is read, so a PR merged the moment CI went green (GitHub auto-merge) still finishes a card that reaches review afterwards.
  - compare results are cached per PR and commit pair. A 404 or an unreadable compare is read again after ten minutes; two failed reads in a row leave one hint, written only if the card is still in review with no step in flight and no completion row this round. A checkpoint that is not a 40-hex sha never reaches the URL or the hint text and takes no anonymous slot. Hints are written once per round and quote branch names as data.
  - Open, unreadable (including a response without a boolean `merged`), or phase changed during a read: nothing is written. A sweep that starts while the last one runs returns at once. Cache rows of PRs that left review or the grind are dropped. The sweep log counts the reconcile (`reviewPending`, `reviewSkipped`, `reviewUnreadable`, `reviewForeign`, `merged`, `closedUnmerged`, `hinted`, `settledBefore`) apart from the grind.
  - Only the build's own PR: before any write the pull's head repository must be its base repository (compared by repository id, so a renamed or transferred repository still matches) and its head ref the build's conversation branch. The daemon finds the PR number with `gh pr list --head <branch>`, which matches the branch name only, so on a public repo a fork PR with the same branch name can be the number on the build. A mismatch, or a head repository that GitHub reports as null (a deleted fork), writes nothing (no done, no failed) and leaves one hint per round; a response without the head ref or the base repository id counts as unreadable and is read again. Text from GitHub that reaches a system row (branch names, the merger's login, the merge sha) is stripped of control characters and cut to 100 characters.
- `apps/server/src/services/builds.ts`: the merge step's done tail moves into `finishTodoDone`, shared by the merge step and the reconcile. It checks that the card can reach done (a person may have closed it while the merge step ran) before touching anything, stops the build's unclaimed verify / review steps, sets done, writes the completion row (`DONE_ROW`, every time, as before), and advances split waves. `roundStart` and `hasMessageRow` back the per-round markers. `requestMerge` and the AI review action re-read the phase after their await and refuse when the reconcile finished the card meanwhile. Step events go through quota-wait's `publishStepRow`. `phase.ts` names the reconcile as a review -> done / failed producer, and `docs/spec/02` §4.2 describes it next to the main sequence and in the failure list.
- `apps/server/src/lib/github.ts`: `githubPull` reads `state`, `merged`, `merge_commit_sha`, `merged_by.login`, `head.sha`, `head.ref`, `head.repo.id`, `base.ref`, `base.repo.id` and `base.repo.default_branch` with `If-None-Match`; `githubPullState` (#931) is now a projection of it. It and `githubCommitCheckRuns` share one conditional GET. `githubCompareStatus` asks for one page and answers `invalid` without a request when either commit is not a 40-hex sha.
- The checks path and the new path share `githubTarget` (which goes through #1468's `githubRepoOfProject`: a `githubRepo` that is not owner/repo, or has a `.` or `..` segment, is refused), `tokenFor` and `hasActiveStep`. Two changes reach the CI grind: its candidates are limited to the todo's current build (since #1150 a newer build in flight still had the old PR ground), an unclaimed verify or review step no longer holds it back, and a step of another kind waiting for quota (a fix step, or a #931 rework build step) counts as in flight, so the grind adds no second fix step behind it. `ci-loop.test.ts`'s fixture now sets `todo.latestBuildId`, which every grind test depends on.

Segments 2 and 3 cover the human merge through the API with `sha`, the review-gate wake text (G9), checks by head SHA, and DIRTY/BEHIND.
