Comments in the test file and `finishTodoDone` state the current rules instead of their history, and spec 02 §4.2 states the anonymous stop rule as the code applies it.

Round 16, after pr-gate run 8 (`go: true` at `deff4b9`, suggestions only; verdict in [pr-gate-1414-run8-deff4b9.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/9ef2a0c4702fd99eeb49afcc4e4747dbf6190eb0/docs/verify/1403/pr-gate-1414-run8-deff4b9.json)), at `bc9c833` ([r16-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/9ef2a0c4702fd99eeb49afcc4e4747dbf6190eb0/docs/verify/1403/r16-red-green.txt), [r16-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/9ef2a0c4702fd99eeb49afcc4e4747dbf6190eb0/docs/verify/1403/r16-mutations.txt), [gates-16.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/9ef2a0c4702fd99eeb49afcc4e4747dbf6190eb0/docs/verify/1403/gates-16.txt)). A close is confirmed only by the read right after the closed read: a sweep that skips the card because a step is in flight, a step that starts during the read, a failed read and a response without the head fields each clear the first sighting, so two short closes with no open read between them no longer fail the card. The anonymous five-minute skip and the budget skip keep it, since anonymous reads are always that far apart. The merge-containment check counts every pushed checkpoint of the build, not only build steps, so a Verifier commit pushed after a GitHub merge leaves the card in review with a hint. `finishTodoDone` has no already-done branch: no production caller reaches it (`completeStep` returns early for a done card, and the reconcile checks review first), and ㉟ now drives a late merge step through `completeStep`. Each review candidate is counted in one bucket every sweep, also once its hint exists. New `PullSpec` options drop `base.ref` or `default_branch` alone, so ㉗ and [61] reach the guard that evicts an incomplete merged response from the cache. With the test files of `3299f2d` against the `deff4b9` sources, 7 of 135 fail; at `bc9c833` pr-reconcile, ci-loop and close-stops-active-steps pass 163 of 163, pr-reconcile and ci-loop pass 20 runs out of 20, and 12 of 12 mutations are caught (deleting the cache eviction at the base guard leaves the round 15 tests green). Gates at `bc9c833`: lint, the warning cap (0), typecheck, spec:parse, `vitest run --changed origin/main` (1304 passed, 1 skipped), the spawn gate and e2e:affected (8 passed) exit 0. The `/code-review` on the round asked whether a second merge step could now reach `finishTodoDone` on a done card; it cannot, and `bc9c833` makes the comment say when a second completion row is written.

Round 17, after pr-gate run 9 (`go: false` at `9ef2a0c`, one blocking finding; verdict in [pr-gate-1414-run9-9ef2a0c.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/f8ab21b83f297233a212c20f0a60910b0a6a6188/docs/verify/1403/pr-gate-1414-run9-9ef2a0c.json)), at `81d5ef1` ([r17-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/f8ab21b83f297233a212c20f0a60910b0a6a6188/docs/verify/1403/r17-red-green.txt), [r17-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/f8ab21b83f297233a212c20f0a60910b0a6a6188/docs/verify/1403/r17-mutations.txt), [gates-17.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/f8ab21b83f297233a212c20f0a60910b0a6a6188/docs/verify/1403/gates-17.txt), [r17-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/f8ab21b83f297233a212c20f0a60910b0a6a6188/docs/verify/1403/r17-reviews.txt)). The finding: the closed path failed the card for any closed same-repository PR from the conversation branch, whatever its base. A second PR from that branch to another base (a collaborator's backport, or an organization member's), recorded on the build by the daemon probe and then closed, failed the card while the build's real PR was still open. One skeptic confirmed the trace; the other found that GitHub requires write access or organization membership to open such a PR, so it is not reachable by any reader of a public repository. The closed path now acts only on a PR whose base is the default branch, the rule the merged path already applied; a closed PR with another base leaves one hint per round after the confirming read and writes nothing else, and a closed response without `base.ref` or `default_branch` is unreadable. The last pushed checkpoint is the step that last checked in (`coalesce(lastHeartbeatAt, claimedAt, createdAt)`), not the one created last, so a verify step created in an earlier round that pushes after a later build step is compared. `githubText` also strips format characters (bidi overrides, zero-width). ⑨b adds the realistic shape of #1217's second build recording an existing PR from the older build's branch: foreign, one hint, card stays in review. With the test files of `be62193` against the `9ef2a0c` sources, 5 of 142 fail; at `81d5ef1` 142 of 142 pass, 10 runs out of 10, and 9 of 9 mutations are caught. Gates at `81d5ef1`: lint, the warning cap, typecheck, spec:parse, the spawn gate and e2e:affected (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` passed on the third run (1311 passed), the first two failing only `skill-write.test.ts` M5 on its 5 s timeout at a load average of about 18 from other lanes (unchanged file, 30 of 30 alone). `/code-review` on the round found nothing.

pr-gate run 10 at `f8ab21b` said go with no blocking finding; its suggestions and where each goes are in a PR comment (segment 2 of #1403 takes the PR-replaced case and the test pins it lists).

Round 18 merges main into the branch after #1468, #1474, #1475, #1421, #1469 and #1476 landed ([r18-merge-main.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/5ac8f41992d35151948f0eef9891f519df8de8a1/docs/verify/1403/r18-merge-main.txt)). The one conflict was in `ci-loop.ts`: the branch keeps `githubTarget` and `tokenFor`, and `githubTarget` now goes through `githubRepoOfProject`, as #1403's segment-2 list says the second of the two PRs to merge does. A new case ㊳b (`../user`, `octo/..`, `./demo`: no request) fails 3 of 3 on the old `githubTarget` and passes on the new one. #1468's own R7b test built its grind candidate without `todo.latestBuildId`, which this PR's grind requires, so it saw no candidate; its fixture now sets the current build, as `ci-loop.test.ts`'s does, and the assertion keeps every grind counter. Gates at `cefad17`: lint, typecheck, spec:parse, `vitest run --changed origin/main` (1420 passed, 1 skipped) and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0.

pr-gate run 11 at `5ac8f41` said go with no blocking finding and five suggestions; the disposition of each is in a PR comment. Three are test pins already on #1403's segment-2 list (a second sweep in ⑱d and ⑱f, `sweepTwice` in ⑧b, the four survivors named on #1403), one is the squash message, which the Issues section already covers, and one is the round 18 test order, recorded in Risk.

One run of the two test files during round 11 failed one ci-loop case (the batch sweep test) on the same tree that then passed 14 runs in a row; the output kept only the test name (`r11-red-green.txt`). pr-gate run 8 found the likely cause: the test helper picked each PR number at random from 900 values and every check-runs mock answered with the same ETag, so two of the three candidates sharing a number (about 0.3% of runs) shared a cache entry. Round 16 numbers them from a counter; forcing the collision on the old helper fails 3 of 3 runs.

Gates at `862bd69` ([gates-9.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/d0ad204b577b2251ebc5abc18c9f660a16e7d2a7/docs/verify/1403/gates-9.txt)): lint (782 files, 1 info), the warning cap (0), typecheck, spec:parse, `vitest run --changed origin/main` (131 files, 1229 passed) and e2e:affected (6 passed) exit 0.

Two ci-loop tests asserted "a review-phase build makes no requests" and "after green, a second sweep makes no requests". They now assert "no check-runs read" and allow the `pulls/{n}` read, which is the point of this change.

Gates, round 1 at `39990ab` ([gates.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/39990abc5fe6a8860f26414a96b640c046240816/docs/verify/1403/gates.txt)), round 3 at `c35c349` (in `fix3-green.txt`) and round 2 at `ea2b9f8` ([gates-2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/ea2b9f883b8962e9de0b99ab8881ed5d6277b705/docs/verify/1403/gates-2.txt), same four gates, all exit 0):

```
$ pnpm lint
Checked 782 files in 1454ms. No fixes applied.
Found 1 info.
$ pnpm typecheck
packages/shared, apps/web, apps/daemon, apps/server, integration typecheck: Done
$ pnpm spec:parse
[spec-parse-gate] PASS: every spec in apps/web/e2e and integration/test parses.
$ pnpm --filter @pacman/web e2e:affected
  6 passed (12.4s)
```

`pnpm exec vitest related --changed` selects no tests by construction (#1415), so the whole server project ran instead; AGENTS.md now names `vitest run --changed`.

## Upstream

No equivalent exists in the current code. `githubPullState` (#931) reads `state` and `merged` for the restart decision without `merge_commit_sha` or ETag; it stays for its two callers. GitHub webhooks for pull_request events would replace the poll, but the server sits inside a tailnet that GitHub cannot reach (ci-loop.ts header), so the poll stays the transport.

## Risk

Two-way door: revert the commits and review-phase builds are ignored again. Blast radius: every GitHub-form todo in review whose current build has a PR gets one conditional GET per minute when GitHub is connected (304 responses to authorized requests do not count against the primary rate limit); without a connection the reconcile stops reading at 20 anonymous requests an hour of its own, or when it and the grind together reach 50 (the grind's reads are counted, not capped). A merged PR whose head differs from the last checkpoint adds one compare read per commit pair. The grind now skips PR builds that are not the todo's current build. A closed PR now moves the todo to `failed`, which a person used to do by hand. The merge step's done path is the same code moved into a function, plus stopping unclaimed gate steps. No migration, no wire change, no UI change. The PR edits `docs/spec/02`, outside the ADR 0021 D4 auto-merge set, so it waits for a user merge.

`/code-review` findings left as they are, with the reason:
- The per-round markers are message rows: `DONE_ROW` and the reconcile's closed text. A structured column would need a migration. If the closed text changes wording later, a card between a reported close and a reopen at that moment would see one more report.
- `DONE_ROW` names the completion row that was already product copy, emoji included; this PR gives the existing string a name and adds no new emoji text.
- `probePullState` in builds.ts (#931) keeps its own target and token code; this PR does not touch that path.
- The message table has no index on `conversationId`; the reconcile keeps positive marker lookups in memory instead of adding one, so a settled or hinted card costs no repeated scans.

`/code-review` findings from the fifth and sixth passes left as they are, with the reason:
- From the seventh pass: when the reconcile fails a card on a closed PR it stops the build's unclaimed verify step. If the PR is then reopened and the card restarted onto the same build (#931 reuse), `maybeEnqueueVerifyStep` finds that stopped row and enqueues no Verifier for the new round. On main that check already skips any build with a verify row, so a second round on one build gets no Verifier today either; verify is advisory, not a merge gate. Making it look at the round belongs with segment 2's rework of the merge path.
- The CI grind (#1150, unchanged here except for the current-build limit and the gate-step rule) reads checks by branch name and does not read the PR's state. A repo that auto-merges and deletes the head branch on merge leaves a card in building (its checks go unreadable), a PR closed during building keeps getting fix rounds until the dead-loop gate, and a grind card whose checks never read keeps adding anonymous reads. Segment 3 reads checks by head SHA and covers these.
- The merged row is written just before `finishTodoDone`, outside a transaction; only a database error between the two would repeat it on the next sweep.
- A PR merged into the old default branch, with the repository renamed before the reconcile reads it, is reported as merged into another branch; the window is one sweep unless the server was down.
- Review candidates are read one after another; with a token, a slow GitHub can push a sweep past 60 s, and the next tick is skipped.
- Close confirmation could read `closed_at` instead of a second read, which compares GitHub's clock with the server's, the kind of rule round 7 removed. The anonymous budget is counted here, not read from GitHub's `x-ratelimit-*` headers, which would also see the #931 / #1217 guard reads.
- The reconcile reads the PR number recorded on the build, which the daemon probe refreshes only when a non-review step finishes. If a person closes the build's PR and opens a new one from the same conversation branch while the card is in review, the closed read fails the card while the new PR is open, and after a restore a merge of the new PR is not seen. Segment 2, which reworks the merge step and the PR identity, takes this; listed on #1403.
- The step table has no completion time, so the last pushed checkpoint is the step that last checked in; two steps of one build that overlap and finish less than 30 s apart (one heartbeat) can be ordered wrongly, which leaves the card in review with a hint rather than finishing it. An exact `finishedAt` needs a migration.
- Round 18's ㊳b was written after the merge that routes `githubTarget` through `githubRepoOfProject`; its red leg swaps the old `githubTarget` back in, so it works as a mutation run rather than a test that came first. The rule itself is #1468's, already tested on main.
- #1468 (#1466) merged first; round 18's merge of main routes `githubTarget` through its `githubRepoOfProject`, so the reconcile and the grind refuse the same stored values the rest of the server does.
- A manual done from review does not stop unclaimed gate steps at the moment of the move. Since #1452 (now on this branch) the scheduler tick stops the pending or quota-waiting steps of a done card and a done from queued, planning or building stops them at once, so the window is one tick; closing it at claim time is outside this PR.
- `tokenFor` decrypts once per candidate per sweep; the number of candidates is the number of PR cards in building or review.
- Round 10 added tests after the rules they cover had shipped (CLAUDE.md asks for tests first); its red leg is the mutation run.
- From pr-gate run 6: a merge step queued for an Agent whose machine is offline counts as in flight (unclaimed steps wait for their machine, #1257), so a PR merged on GitHub meanwhile is reported only when that machine returns and its merge step runs. Nothing wrong is written and main never reports it; segment 2 reworks the merge step.
- The ownership check reads the PR the daemon recorded. The daemon's `gh pr list --head <branch>` probe (`apps/daemon/src/github-probe.ts`) still matches by branch name; the REST path already uses `owner:branch`. Filtering the probe by owner is a follow-up outside this PR. Until then a build whose recorded PR is a fork's stays in review with the hint, and a PR the agent opened from a branch other than the conversation branch is treated the same way, the safe direction. `mergedPrElsewhere` (#1217) also reads the recorded PR number and is not changed here.
- From pr-gate run 7: a foreign PR that is closed stays a conditional read every sweep (a 304 when nothing changed); treating it as final like a merged PR would need a rule for a PR whose base or head is later edited, so it stays a read. The live fixtures were read through this container's proxy, which adds its own GitHub credentials, so they show response shapes, not the anonymous rate limit. Some round 14 and 15 tests pin rules that were already in place (CLAUDE.md asks for tests first); their red leg is the mutation run.

Decided by the user on 2026-10-21 (option B; the `needs-decision` label is removed): pr-gate run 5 traced one path where a merge on GitHub goes unreported. In GitHub form the merge step can finish without merging the PR (it merges the default branch into the PR branch and pushes; merging the PR is left to the agent's prompt, #1403 "Current state"). The completion row it writes is this round's marker. If a person then moves the card back to review and merges the PR on GitHub, the reconcile finds the marker and leaves the card in review with no merged row (⑱c pins that a reopen after the merge step stays). Segment 2 makes the merge step merge the PR through the API with `sha`, so its completion row then always means the PR is merged; this PR adds no rule for the case.

## Acceptance

- [x] Merged, closed and open PR states handled (pr-reconcile ①②③; `green.txt`)
- [x] Unreadable reads and phase races write nothing (④ 429/404/502, ⑤; `green.txt`)
- [x] Older superseded PR builds do not move the todo, also when the current build has no PR (⑥, ⑧a, ⑧b; `fix-green.txt`)
- [x] An in-flight merge step is left alone (⑩a); a second merge step in one round writes its own completion row ([54])
- [x] lint / typecheck / spec:parse / e2e:affected pass at each round's head (`gates.txt`, `gates-2.txt`, `fix3-green.txt`, `gates-4.txt` to `gates-17.txt`; `gates-17.txt` at `81d5ef1`; round 18 at `cefad17` in `r18-merge-main.txt`)
- [x] A merge that missed the build's last commit leaves the todo in review with a hint (⑭a-c; `fix3-green.txt`)
- [x] Each outcome reported once per round: a reopen after the report stays, a rework round starts fresh, a merge before review entry still finishes the card, a merge outside the default branch leaves a hint (⑱, ⑲, ㉝, ㉞; `r7-red-green.txt`)
- [x] Unclaimed (queued or quota-blocked) gate steps stopped on the reconcile's finish and the merge step's finish (a manual done from review relies on the scheduler tick of #1452, see Risk); merge and review actions refuse after a concurrent finish (⑮c, ⑳, ㉖, ㉖b, ㊺)
- [x] Request budget: one sweep at a time, per-PR and process-wide anonymous limits shared fairly, compare backoff (⑪, ㉑, ㊱, ㊴, ㊸, ㊹, ㊻)
- [x] Round 9 rules: 37 of 37 mutations caught (`r9-mutations.txt`)
- [x] Round 10: the grind's gate-step rule and the compare-hint recheck held by tests, 2 of 2 mutations caught (`r10-mutations.txt`); gates at `0c5a702` (`gates-10.txt`)
- [x] Rounds 11 to 13: close confirmed over two reads, budgets split between the reconcile and the grind, done doc without a stale quota chip, merged PRs not re-read unless the response was incomplete, transition checked first; 23 of 23 mutations caught; gates at `f9f5a2f` (`r11-*`, `r12-*`, `r13-*`, `gates-13.txt`)
- [x] Round 14: a fork PR or another branch's PR recorded on the build neither finishes nor fails the card, a response without the head fields is read again, the merge step's done path and the grind's quota-waiting rule pinned; 4 of 4 mutations caught (`r14-red-green.txt`, `r14-mutations.txt`, `gates-14.txt`)
- [x] Round 15: ownership by repository id (renames and transfers keep working, a deleted fork is foreign), GitHub text bounded, parsers checked against live responses, head-sha guard, `behind` and split waves pinned; 22 of 22 mutations caught on the head sources (`r15-red-green.txt`, `r15-mutations.txt`, `r15-live-capture.txt`, `gates-15.txt`)
- [x] Round 16: a close confirmed only by the next read, every pushed checkpoint in the containment check, no already-done branch in the done funnel, one tally bucket per candidate, the base guard reached by tests, the batch sweep test without random PR numbers; 12 of 12 mutations caught (`r16-red-green.txt`, `r16-mutations.txt`, `gates-16.txt`)
- [x] Round 17: a closed PR acts only when its base is the default branch, checkpoints ordered by when the step last checked in, format characters stripped, the realistic #1217 shape pinned; 9 of 9 mutations caught (`r17-red-green.txt`, `r17-mutations.txt`, `gates-17.txt`)

Host leg, not a task here: a PR merged in the GitHub UI moving its card to done within a minute on mea waits for the long-lived host (spec 28 §8 「待宿主」); segment 3 records a live read against the public repo from this container.

## Issues

Part of #1403, segment 1 of 3. Segment 3 carries the closing line for #1403; this squash body has no closing keyword for it.

The branch's commit messages describe each round's rule, and later rounds replaced earlier ones, so the first commit's message (what `.[0].commit.message` returns) does not describe the code at the head. Squash with this message instead:

```
server(1403): reconcile review-phase PRs merged or closed on GitHub (#1414)

A GitHub-form todo in review now learns what happened to its PR. The
ci-loop sweep reads pulls/{n} for the todo's current build when no
step is in flight (conditional GET, not repeated once read as merged
with the fields the merge check needs; without
a GitHub connection every five minutes per PR; the reconcile stops
at 20 anonymous requests an hour of its own, or at 50 with the
grind).

- Merged into the default branch, with the merged head containing the
  build's last pushed checkpoint: a merged row, then the same done
  finish as the merge step. A merge into another branch or one that
  missed a later commit leaves the card in review with one hint.
- Closed without merge into the default branch and still closed at the
  next read, 50 s or more later: a closed row, build.errorMessage,
  failed. A closed PR with another base leaves one hint.
- Each outcome is reported once per round (round = the build's latest
  build or plan step), so a person's move back to review stays.
- finishTodoDone checks the transition first, stops unclaimed verify /
  review steps before publishing done, and writes the completion row;
  requestMerge and the AI review action re-read the phase after their
  await.
- Only the build's own PR counts: the head repository must be the
  base repository (by id) and the head ref the conversation branch;
  otherwise nothing is written and one hint is left. GitHub text in
  system rows is bounded.
- The CI grind takes only the todo's current build, and an unclaimed
  verify or review step no longer holds it back.
- githubTarget goes through githubRepoOfProject, so the reconcile and
  the grind refuse a githubRepo with a . or .. segment (#1466).
- docs/spec/02 §4.2 describes the reconcile.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_012odUHNQRa4CWjzR22iWH8s
```

mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment 2, the last, of #1402 (bootstrap phase P1, the verify-pacman CLI; `docs/spec/28` §4 P1). Segment 1 (#1411, `vp.mjs` and `vp-registry.json`) is on main as `e1b051a`. This segment adds the registry gate, puts the `vp.mjs drive` commands into the feature maps, and takes the items pr-gate run 9 on #1411 left for it (https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1402#issuecomment-6314487263).

- `.claude/skills/verify-pacman/scripts/vp-registry-gate.mjs` (stdlib only) fails when:
  - a file in `scripts/` is neither a case script nor a `support` entry;
  - a `drive-<number>` script is not one of the 61 that exist today, registered or not (the ticket's rule: new probes are named for the feature);
  - the registry has no case;
  - a case script, support file or recipe path does not exist, or a status or need is unknown;
  - an `evidence.writes` path inside `docs/verify` lacks `rewrites-evidence`;
  - a `vp.mjs drive` line in a feature map names an unregistered case, or a feature with a recipe has no drive line.

  A self-test case runs it on this checkout, so the existing CI self-test step enforces it.
- The 35 feature maps with a recipe end their "How to get to it (user POV)" section with full `node .claude/skills/verify-pacman/scripts/vp.mjs drive <feature> <case>` commands for current cases and what each needs. Stale cases are listed with the reason `drive` refuses them, and a map whose feature has no current case says so. `glass-journeys.md` has a drive line per journey; `review-700.md` and `skill-import.md` gain the user-path section they lacked.
- `vp.mjs` also refuses an evidence directory inside the `docs/verify` of any `git worktree list` entry, read from the caller's directory, from `VERIFY_REPO_ROOT` and from `vp.mjs`'s own checkout, so main's `vp.mjs` run from a sibling worktree cannot overwrite that worktree's archived evidence. `docs/verify-notes` and the like stay allowed.
- Cases whose verdict depends on the stack's state are marked in the registry and `drive` checks the marks. `fresh-stack` (13 cases, `api-keys/create`, `machine-stale-sweep` and `search/project-line` among them): once a drive is recorded on the stack (`VERIFY_RUN_DIR/vp-drives.txt`, written after doctor passes, cleared by launch and cleanup), such a case is refused with "cleanup, then launch", and `--force` overrides. `own-stack` (the 7 glass cases): refused while a stack's `ports.json` is in `VERIFY_RUN_DIR`, also with `--force`.
- The optional-seed exemption in the self-test covers only a seed the usage names inside "(optional …)", not the whole case.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the self-test after "Spec parse gate (#1052)" and before "Install Playwright chromium", so the spec-parse comment's "first signal after install" holds again.
- Four probe headers say `vp.mjs archive` instead of `cp`; spec 28 §4 P1 says `archive` copies and `links` prints the raw links after the push, and §8 records P0 and P1. `docs/verify/1402/README.md` indexes every evidence directory of both segments with its round, commit and leg.
- `SKILL.md`, `features/README.md`, the Cursor flow step 4 and the changelog (`2026-10-20-1402.md`, segment 2 section) describe the marks and the gate.

## Verified

Failure modes first ([seg2-failure-modes.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/8dc909ae06eb60014f5ace04d0ddb6a462c242e9/docs/verify/1402/seg2-failure-modes.txt)). The self-test cases on `c3f22bc` (tests only) against main's `vp.mjs` and registry read 54/66: 12 of the 13 new cases fail, and the `VERIFY_WEB_PORT` pin passes because main already refuses a mismatched web port. At `87480f0` and `2ddff26` they read 66/66 on Node 22 and Node 24 ([seg2-selftest.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/8dc909ae06eb60014f5ace04d0ddb6a462c242e9/docs/verify/1402/seg2-selftest.txt)).

Live, using only `vp.mjs --help` and the maps' drive lines on a fresh stack at 8791 / 5273 ([seg2-live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/8dc909ae06eb60014f5ace04d0ddb6a462c242e9/docs/verify/1402/seg2-live.txt)):

- `api-keys create` 6/6, `search search` 2/2 and `theme persist` 2/2 pass.
- On the same stack a second `api-keys create` and `glass-journeys create-task` (also with `--force`) exit 2 with their reasons; after `cleanup`, `create-task` passes 3/3 on its own stack.
- The runs were archived with `vp.mjs archive 1402 --from …` into four directories; repeating an archive is refused; `vp.mjs links 1402` printed the links after the commit.
- pr-gate run 9's add-only case, replayed with `--dry-run` from a sibling worktree: main's `vp.mjs` targets that worktree's archived directory (exit 0), this branch's refuses it (exit 2).

The negative control (ticket acceptance 3) is segment 1's; the README links it.

27 mutations, each run in a scratch copy, are each caught ([seg2-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/8dc909ae06eb60014f5ace04d0ddb6a462c242e9/docs/verify/1402/seg2-mutations.txt)). The first pass caught 26: reading the worktree list only from `vp.mjs`'s repository passed because the test's caller and `vp.mjs` shared one repository. `668e79c` adds a second clone as the caller, and that mutation is red.

Gates at `87480f0` and `2ddff26` ([gates-seg2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/8dc909ae06eb60014f5ace04d0ddb6a462c242e9/docs/verify/1402/gates-seg2.txt)): `pnpm lint` (the existing info in `machines-page.tsx:317`), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, the self-test, the feature-map staleness gate (334 references, baseline unchanged), the registry gate, `vitest run --changed origin/main` (no file selected) and `e2e:affected` (no web surface) exit 0. `/code-review` at low effort, run twice, and `/simplify` (a shared worktree helper in the self-test, a derived support list, duplicate roots skipped before git runs) are in [seg2-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/8dc909ae06eb60014f5ace04d0ddb6a462c242e9/docs/verify/1402/seg2-reviews.txt); neither review read the self-test's own hunks, which the mutations cover.

## Upstream

No dependency. The gate uses only Node's standard library; `git worktree list --porcelain` gives the worktree roots.

## Risk

Two-way door. A new `drive-<number>.mjs` now fails CI even when registered; a probe is named for its feature. If main gains another `drive-<number>` script before this merges, the gate fails until that script is renamed or added to the frozen list. A fresh-stack case can need `cleanup` and `launch` between drives where it used to run and fail; `--force` keeps the old behavior. `vp.mjs` runs `git worktree list` only when an evidence directory has to be checked.

`03-keys-once.png` in the new `api-keys` run shows the one-time plaintext of a key minted on a scratch stack that `vp.mjs cleanup` deleted; it authenticates nothing, as in segment 1.

The patch is 2,226 lines (898 outside `docs/verify/`) across 70 files and touches `.claude/**`, `.cursor/**`, `.github/**` and `docs/spec/**`, so under ADR 0021 D4 it waits for a user merge.

mergedPulls.title: server(1404): merge gate S3, gate tables migration
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment S3 of #1404 (bootstrap phase P3, the merge-readiness gate; plan in https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1404#issuecomment-6304303150). One migration, `apps/server/drizzle/0044_merge_gate_tables.sql`, adds the four server-owned tables the later segments write and read. Nothing writes to them yet.

- `gate_digest`, primary key (`buildId`, `headSha`): the patch digest S1 computes for a build's PR at one head (`patchDigest`, the counted and kept file and line totals the D4 size caps use). A new head after update-branch gets its own row.
- `gate_round`, one row per review round, UNIQUE (`buildId`, `patchDigest`) and UNIQUE (`buildId`, `round`): the round number, which `[review-fix]` round produced the patch, the frozen perspectives, the perspectives that timed out, dispatch counts per kind and perspective with the last dispatch time, and the round state (`open`, `fixing`, `fix_no_change`, `closed`). These are the fields S2's readiness reads and S7 will coordinate.
- `gate_verdict`, primary key `stepId` (no foreign key to `step`), indexed by `buildId`: kind, perspective, outcome and `patchDigest` as S2's `GateVerdictView` carries them (a null digest counts toward no patch), the head the step reported and the head the server pinned at dispatch (`expectedHeadSha`, not null). `stepId` has no foreign key, as `plan`, `steer_pending` and `stop_pending` have none: drizzle runs migrations inside a transaction, where `PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF` has no effect, so a cascade from `step` would delete every verdict whenever a later migration recreates `step`, and a step deleted without its build would take a recorded block with it. Verdicts live here and not in message rows, because the machine transcript upload accepts any role and id (plan fact 1); nothing on the machine upload path refers to these tables.
- `gate_state`, primary key `buildId`: the latest readiness snapshot (ready, head, digest, policy, blockers as JSON).
- Every `buildId` is a foreign key to `build` with on-delete cascade, as `plan` and `branch_sync` have. The tables are registered in `DB_TABLES` and `INTERNAL_ONLY_TABLES` (`packages/shared/src/tables.ts`). Column comments in `schema.ts` name the S1 or S2 type each column holds; the value lists are `$type` literals without CHECK constraints, as elsewhere in the schema.

## Verified

Failure modes first ([s3-failure-modes.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/333001043462ce8e9392910b12d4056a30141019/docs/verify/1404/s3-failure-modes.txt)). The new tests against main's schema fail 22 of 141 (19 of the 20 new tests plus the table registry, vocabulary and snapshot tests); on the branch 141 of 141 pass ([s3-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/333001043462ce8e9392910b12d4056a30141019/docs/verify/1404/s3-red-green.txt)). The one new test that passes on main checks that the machine upload code does not refer to the gate tables, which holds before and after. The tests find the migration by content, not number, and check that its journal `when` is later than every earlier entry, since drizzle skips a migration whose `when` is not newer than the last one applied.

Live ([s3-live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/333001043462ce8e9392910b12d4056a30141019/docs/verify/1404/s3-live.txt), servers on 8795 and 8796 with scratch homes, read with better-sqlite3):

- Main's server (`2294b08`) made a database with 44 migrations, 31 tables and a project, task and build; this branch's server then started on the same home and applied 0044 (45 migrations, 35 tables), the build row intact, and gate rows could be written for it.
- A second (`buildId`, `patchDigest`) or (`buildId`, `round`) fails on the unique index; a second `stepId`, `gate_state` or `gate_digest` row fails on the primary key; a verdict for a missing step failed on the foreign key. That last claim is round 1 only: round 2 removed the `stepId` foreign key (commit 2136fea), F5 at the head asserts that such a verdict is stored, and the live evidence for the head is [s3-r2-live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/s3-r2-live.txt).
- `DELETE /api/todos/:id` (204), `POST /api/todos/:id/reset` (200, the other build's rows untouched) and `DELETE /api/projects/:id` (204) each leave no gate rows for the removed builds. At the head, `s3-r2-live.txt` covers `DELETE /api/todos/:id` live; reset and project delete at the head rest on the F7 tests.

Round 1: eight mutations, each with the migration regenerated by drizzle-kit, are each caught ([s3-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/333001043462ce8e9392910b12d4056a30141019/docs/verify/1404/s3-mutations.txt)): either unique index removed, `patchDigest` not null, no cascade on the verdict's build or step, no foreign key on `gate_state`, the step foreign key dropped, the journal `when` set below 0043's. Two of these (no cascade on the verdict's step, the step foreign key dropped) concern the `stepId` foreign key that round 2 removed, so they no longer apply to the head; the step foreign key dropped is now the shipped schema.

Gates ([gates-s3.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/333001043462ce8e9392910b12d4056a30141019/docs/verify/1404/gates-s3.txt)): `pnpm lint` (the existing info in `machines-page.tsx:317`), the warning cap, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, the spawn gate, `db:check`, `db:generate` with no new migration, the feature-map staleness gate and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` passes 2456 with the one root-only failure (`runner-brief.test.ts` "擦除失败": `chmodSync(cwd, 0o500)` does nothing for root; CI runs as a normal user). `/code-review` at low effort on `origin/main..claude/bootstrap-p3c` found nothing.

Round 2, after pr-gate run 1 (go at `3330010`, suggestions only; verdict in [pr-gate-1469-run1-3330010.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/pr-gate-1469-run1-3330010.json)), at `4d37bfe` ([s3-r2-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/s3-r2-red-green.txt), [s3-r2-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/s3-r2-mutations.txt), [s3-r2-live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/s3-r2-live.txt), [s3-r2-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/s3-r2-reviews.txt), [gates-s3-2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/gates-s3-2.txt)). The run showed that the `stepId` foreign key with cascade would let a drizzle-shaped recreate of `step` wipe every verdict; it is gone, and 0044 is regenerated with only that line removed. New tests: a recreate of `step` after the gate migration keeps every verdict (F17); a step deleted without its build keeps its verdict (F18); every migration after the gate migration keeps the gate rows (F19, with mutations that recreate `build` or `todo` showing it red); null `expectedHeadSha` and null round digest are refused (F20, F21). The upgrade test seeds the old database with SQL instead of the head's `seed()`. Red 3 of 146 on `f859a18` (tests only), green 146 of 146; 12 mutations that go red plus 2 controls that stay green (one moves gate rows aside around a `build` recreate, the other recreates `step`). Live, main's server made a database, this branch's server upgraded it: `gate_verdict` has one foreign key (`buildId`), a verdict on a missing step is stored, deleting the step keeps it, and deleting the task clears all four tables (that live run covers `DELETE /api/todos/:id`; reset and project delete rest on the F7 tests). `/simplify` folded the table counts into one query; `/code-review` at medium effort on the branch's three-dot diff, test file included, raised 9 points: one comment fixed, the rest kept with their reasons in `s3-r2-reviews.txt`. Gates at `34381bd`: lint, the warning cap, typecheck, spec:parse, the spawn gate, `db:check`, `db:generate` with no change and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` had the root-only runner-brief case and one `skill-write` timeout under a load of 24 on 4 CPUs, which passes 30 of 30 alone. `4d37bfe` changes one schema comment.

pr-gate run 2 at `4d37bfe` returned go with 0 blocking and 8 suggestions, all handled in this body (Verified, Risk, Issues and Acceptance); the dispositions are in a comment on this PR, and the verdict JSON is kept in the session scratchpad, not committed.

## Upstream

No dependency. drizzle-kit generates the migration, journal entry and snapshot with the repo's `db:generate`; `db:check` passes.

## Risk

Two-way door at the code level, one-way for a database that ran it: SQLite keeps the tables after a revert, and a later 0044 from another branch would collide with this number. CLAUDE.md numbers migrations at merge time, so if main gains a 0044 first this branch regenerates its migration under the next number; the tests do not depend on the number.

The columns are the plan's plus a few later segments will need (`gate_verdict.headSha`, `gate_round`'s second unique index, `fixRound`, `perspectives`, `timedOut`, `dispatches`); the round `state` list is a proposal for S7. S1 writes digests as `pd2:<hex>` now; the column is plain text. `keptLines` is the sum of additions and deletions over S1's kept files, since S1 exposes no such total. A step dispatched without a pinned head gets no verdict row (`expectedHeadSha` is not null). A later migration that recreates `build`, or `todo` (which cascades into `build`), must move the gate rows aside and back, as the schema comment and F19 say; making `migrate` run with foreign keys off is a separate change to `db/client.ts`; where S5a stores the pinned head at dispatch is S5a's choice. The table list in spec 01 §6 is historical and already misses several tables, so it is not edited; `DB_TABLES` is the maintained list.

Kept unfixed from the round-2 `/code-review` (reasons in [s3-r2-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/s3-r2-reviews.txt)):

- Point 7: F15 is a text check over `routes-machine.ts` and `services/machine*.ts`, so it also passes on main; the behavioural guard comes with S5a's writer.
- Point 8: `memory()` in the test never closes its handle and runs the 45 migrations per test; in-memory handles are released when the vitest worker for the file exits, the test needs the raw handle that `openDbWithHandle` does not return, and a fresh database per test is the isolation the tests use.
- Point 9: F7 calls `s.dispose()` after its assertions, not in `finally`; the rest of `apps/server/test` does the same (432 call sites) and each test boots its own in-memory server, so a failed assertion cannot leak state into another test's database.

Test limits at this head: F19 runs no later migration (0044 is the last journal entry), and the kind and outcome test copies S2's value lists by hand, so both bite only when a later migration is added or S2's lists change; S5a and later segments carry behavioural tests.

The schema comment at `apps/server/src/db/schema.ts` lines 769-772 and 787-788 names S2's `readiness.ts` and `MERGE_BLOCKERS` / `BLOCKER_CLASSES` / `mergeBlockerSchema`, which land with #1421; until #1421 merges those names are not on main.

The patch is 5,640 lines (about 3,100 of them the generated drizzle snapshot) across 20 files and touches `apps/server/drizzle/**`, so under ADR 0021 D4 it waits for a user merge.

## Acceptance

- [x] Four gate tables with the keys the plan names, cascading with their build (`merge-gate-tables.test.ts`, `s3-live.txt`)
- [x] Main's database upgrades in place; constraints and deletes shown on a live server: evidence for the head is [s3-r2-live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/4d37bfeaeea51228b1714842e6f717180eacecd2/docs/verify/1404/s3-r2-live.txt) (no `stepId` foreign key; `DELETE /api/todos/:id` live, reset and project delete on the F7 tests); [s3-live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/333001043462ce8e9392910b12d4056a30141019/docs/verify/1404/s3-live.txt) is the round-1 record, which predates the foreign key removal
- [x] Round 1: 8 of 8 mutations caught (two of them about the removed `stepId` foreign key); round 2: 12 mutations that go red plus 2 controls that stay green (`s3-mutations.txt`, `s3-r2-mutations.txt`)
- [x] Verdicts survive a recreate of `step` and a step delete; gate rows survive later migrations (`s3-r2-red-green.txt`, `s3-r2-live.txt`)
- [x] lint / typecheck / spec:parse / vitest --changed / e2e:affected / db:check pass, except the root-only runner-brief case; `gates-s3-2.txt` also records the `skill-write` M5 timeout under load (5000 ms limit, the case took 9414 ms at a load average of 19 to 24 on 4 CPUs), which passed 30 of 30 when run alone (`gates-s3.txt`, `gates-s3-2.txt`)

## Issues

Part of #1404, segment S3. The last P3 segment carries the closing line for #1404; this squash body has no closing keyword for it.

The first commit's message (2662c3b0) still describes `gate_verdict` with a foreign key to `step`, which round 2 removed, so the squash must use the "Squash with this message" block in this body, not the first commit's message.

Squash with this message:

```

Migration 0044 adds gate_digest (buildId, headSha), gate_round (one
row per build and patch digest, unique round number), gate_verdict
(one row per step, no foreign key to step; verdicts are not read from
message rows) and gate_state (latest readiness per build). Every
buildId cascades with its build. Nothing writes to them yet.

Part of #1404 (segment S3).
```

mergedPulls.title: server(1404): merge gate S2, mergeReadiness and the blocker vocabulary
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment S2 of #1404 (bootstrap phase P3, the merge readiness gate), on top of S1 (#1420, on main as `9eefe88`). The segment plan is in the ticket comment (https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1404#issuecomment-6304303150). This segment adds the blocker vocabulary and one pure function, `mergeReadiness`. Nothing calls it yet; S6a wires it in as an observer.

- `packages/shared/src/records/merge-gate.ts` gains `MERGE_BLOCKERS`: 50 codes in a fixed order, each with a class (`policy`, `transient` or `human`) and a Chinese label, plus `mergeBlockerSchema` and `mergeReadinessSchema` (`ready`, `headSha`, `patchDigest`, `policy`, `blockers`). The order is the order the status description and the detail page will show.
- `apps/server/src/services/merge-gate/readiness.ts` has `mergeReadiness(inputs)`. The inputs are facts the I/O shell reads (S4/S5): policy and pause, the build lane, the PR, checks on the current head (with a flag that the lists were read in full), the compare (its files and this PR's commits), verdicts with the digest each one is bound to, the round, and which perspectives, verifier and decider the team has. It reads no database, sends no request and takes no clock. The rules from the design:
  - an input it cannot read is a transient blocker, not a skip (`pr-unreadable`, also for a default branch it cannot read; `required-checks-unreadable`; `patch-unavailable` when the compare cannot be read; `mergeable-state` while GitHub is still computing; a check list not read in full counts as unreadable, since a missing check may sit on the page not read); a patch it read but cannot bind waits for a person instead (`compare-truncated`, `compare-malformed` when the compare response has the wrong shape, and `patch-unbindable` when only evidence changed or a file has no blob sha);
  - every blocker is listed, sorted by the vocabulary, so the same inputs give the same first blocker;
  - verdicts count only at the current patch digest; a verdict on an old digest or not bound to a head counts as missing; a later pass at the same digest clears an earlier extraction failure or invalid evidence; a tampered verdict on any digest of the build blocks until a new build, since a new patch does not undo a tamper;
  - a blocking review blocks even when chief said go, and a later pass from the same perspective does not clear it;
  - a missing required check blocks (ci-loop treats it as a grace period, the gate does not); a required check can come from a check run or a commit status; `neutral` and `skipped` pass a required check as branch protection does, while `pr-evidence` must be `success`;
  - any non-passing check other than the gate's own `pacman/merge-gate` status blocks (`mergeable-state`) even when GitHub still reports `clean` or `has_hooks`, because the function's own check list is read later than GitHub computes the state; `unstable` passes only when at least one non-passing check is visible and all of them are the gate's own status, so the gate does not block on itself; `pacman/merge-gate` set as a required check is its own blocker;
  - size cap 800 lines or 40 files over the whole patch, evidence included (ADR 0021 D4 as amended on #1410), from S1's counts; the D4 path classes from S1's `classifyPaths`, including `opaque-file` for a file outside `docs/verify/` that GitHub sent without a patch (a binary file, a very large diff or a pure rename); a raw evidence link counts only when its sha is one of this PR's commits (from the same compare response) and its path is a file this PR adds or changes under this ticket's directory; without a compare the link check is skipped, because the compare blocker already stops the merge.

## Verified

Old leg: the test file before `readiness.ts` existed ([s2-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/97a1f76d003f59f7c2a74eae7ab86cc30c4ba467/docs/verify/1404/s2-red-green.txt)):

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run apps/server/test/merge-gate-readiness.test.ts
 FAIL  |@xiechimon/pacman| test/merge-gate-readiness.test.ts
Error: Cannot find module '../src/services/merge-gate/readiness.js'
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
```

New leg at `97a1f76`:

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run apps/server/test/merge-gate-readiness.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  68 passed (68)
```

The tests start from one all-green input and flip one fact per row, one row for each of the 47 codes; a completeness test fails when a code has no row. Further tests cover the combinations the design names: chief go next to a blocking review, a pass after a block, verdicts on an old or unbound digest, the gate's own status making the PR unstable, a foreign check doing so, a required check from a commit status, `neutral` on `pr-evidence`, unknown ancestry, the frozen round perspectives, ordering, and the 800 / 40 boundaries.

Mutation round 1 ran 19 mutations of `readiness.ts`; two survived ([s2-mutations-1.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/97a1f76d003f59f7c2a74eae7ab86cc30c4ba467/docs/verify/1404/s2-mutations-1.txt)): treating a null `mergeable_state` like any other non-clean state, and counting a failed verify step as a verdict. One test was added and one tightened; round 2 catches 19 of 19 ([s2-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/97a1f76d003f59f7c2a74eae7ab86cc30c4ba467/docs/verify/1404/s2-mutations.txt), definitions at the end of the file):

```
chief go silences blocking                    3 failed | 65 passed (68)
verdicts on any digest count                  1 failed | 67 passed (68)
own status unstable blocks                    1 failed | 67 passed (68)
missing required check is green               1 failed | 67 passed (68)
unknown ancestry counts                       1 failed | 67 passed (68)
mergeable null accepted                       1 failed | 67 passed (68)
failed verify step counts as a verdict        1 failed | 67 passed (68)
...
```

Gates ([gates-s2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/97a1f76d003f59f7c2a74eae7ab86cc30c4ba467/docs/verify/1404/gates-s2.txt)): `pnpm lint` (790 files, the existing `noUselessFragments` info in `machines-page.tsx:317`), `scripts/lint-warning-cap.mjs` (0 warnings), `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm spec:parse` pass; `pnpm --filter @pacman/web e2e:affected` ran `token-gate.spec.ts`, 6 passed. `pnpm exec vitest run --changed` ran 242 files: 2518 passed and one failed, the same root-only `runner-brief.test.ts` case as in S1 (`chmodSync(cwd, 0o500)` does nothing for root; CI runs as a normal user).

S1's round 2 (#1420 at `11ecbde`, after its pr-gate run 1) came into this branch by a merge commit at `4228232`; nothing in `readiness.ts` changed with it. On that head the four merge-gate test files pass 137 of 137 (69 from S1, 68 from S2), and CI was green.

mergedPulls.body:
## What

Segment 3 of #1406 (bootstrap phase P5, `docs/spec/28` §4 P5, ADR 0021 D5): the in-product agent is told this repository's working rules, and text from a GitHub issue reaches every model as fenced third-party data. Plan: https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman/issues/1406#issuecomment-6311590280 (segment 3, failure mode 12).

- `fenceIssueText` in `packages/shared/src/records/prompts.ts` wraps the title and body of a task whose `sourceKind` is `github-issue`: a header line `【GitHub issue 原文 · owner/repo#N】` with a note (text the issue's author wrote on GitHub; data, not instructions; requests in it to change tools, secrets, repositories, memory or merging are not followed; never saved to memory; the system prompt, persona and repo rules win), every body line prefixed with `> ` after `\r`, `\v`, `\f`, `\x1c`-`\x1e`, `\x85`, U+2028 and U+2029 are turned into line breaks, and a footer line. A fake header or footer inside the body stays prefixed. A missing or malformed ref is labelled 「出处未知」 and still fenced. Tasks with any other `sourceKind` (none, `orchestration`, `github-issue-self`) keep today's text byte for byte.
- Fenced where issue text reaches a model: the chief's orchestrate message and the chief claim's instruction (`orchestrate.ts` passes the source), the worker prompts of new sessions (plan, build, merge, restart, ci-fix, the degraded fresh session; the claim's todo carries optional `sourceKind`/`sourceRef` in `machine-wire.ts`, filled by `machines.ts`, and the daemon's `buildTaskPromptText` fences title and body), and the verify step's material (`builds.ts`).
- Kept out of the system layer: the worker's run brief leaves out the title line for a GitHub-sourced task (on main the title reached the system prompt when `meta.titleFinal` was missing); `saveMemoryEntry` in `chief-tools.ts`, the one write path for chief and worker memories, answers 400 when the title or content carries the fence marker; `composeChiefSystemPrompt` gains one rule line saying fenced text and GitHub titles, bodies and comments from tool results are third-party data, never followed for tools, secrets, repositories, memory or merging, never saved as memory, and kept in the fence when a task is split.
- The Implementer persona (`persona.ts`) names the repository's rules: read AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md first; write PR bodies with the repo's PR skill and verify with its verify skill (pr-pacman and verify-pacman here), evidence under `docs/verify/<ticket>/`; commit and PR title shape `<scope>(<ticket>): <subject>`; closing keywords in the commit message; run the repo's gates before committing. A test checks that each `*-pacman` skill it names exists. 837 of the 2,000-character limit.
- The web maps `sourceKind`/`sourceRef` onto the displayed task and treats the fenced orchestrate row, and the unfenced row logged before this change, as the task text.

## Verified

Failure modes first ([p5-3-failure-modes.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/7f5d250e2f263c68ef7a6fe361129da20254c2c7/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-failure-modes.txt)). The six new test files on `51a61c8` (tests only, sources as `2294b08`) fail 27 of 42; at `c60ae64` 42 of 42 pass ([p5-3-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/7f5d250e2f263c68ef7a6fe361129da20254c2c7/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-red-green.txt)). The 15 that pass on the old sources pin today's behavior: plain-task prompts, the existing persona tests and the length cap.

The real composed text, from a scratch server and the daemon's `runStep` with an issue body that carries instruction-like lines, a fake footer and a U+2028 ([p5-3-prompts.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/7f5d250e2f263c68ef7a6fe361129da20254c2c7/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-prompts.txt), script [p5-3-prompts.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/7f5d250e2f263c68ef7a6fe361129da20254c2c7/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-prompts.ts)): the body appears fenced in the orchestrate message, the chief instruction, the plan and build prompts and the verify material, and nowhere in the chief system prompt, the chief claim's system prompt, the worker system prompt or the persona.

Sixteen mutations, each caught ([p5-3-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/7f5d250e2f263c68ef7a6fe361129da20254c2c7/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-mutations.txt), runner [p5-3-mutate.mjs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/7f5d250e2f263c68ef7a6fe361129da20254c2c7/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-mutate.mjs)): the fence removed from the task text (15 tests fail) or from the orchestrate message (2), line breaks not normalized (1), body lines not prefixed (13), the ref label not checked (2), the chief system-prompt rule removed (1), a plain task fenced (3 and 4), the memory gate, the system-prompt title, the claim source, the orchestrate source, the verify material, the two web mappings and a persona naming a skill that does not exist.

Gates at `c60ae64` ([gates-p5-3.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/7f5d250e2f263c68ef7a6fe361129da20254c2c7/docs/verify/1406/gates-p5-3.txt)): `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse` and the spawn gate exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` passes 2516 with the root-only runner-brief case (which #1456 has since made safe as root; it passes on a trial merge with main). The web change runs the full e2e suite through `e2e:affected`: 1180 passed and one failed, `composer-inline-mention.spec.ts:671` waiting 5 s for a chip animation attribute, which passed 96 of 96 in three reruns on the same port. A trial merge with main at `dabef48` has no conflicts and passes typecheck, lint and 202 tests across 13 files. `/code-review` at low effort found nothing. `/security-review` (AGENTS.md lists `machines.ts`) found nothing at its threshold ([p5-3-security-review.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/7f5d250e2f263c68ef7a6fe361129da20254c2c7/docs/verify/1406/p5-3-security-review.txt)).

## Upstream

No dependency. The claim's todo gains two optional fields typed as plain strings, so an older daemon parses a newer claim and a future `sourceKind` does not break it; the wire snapshot records the two fields.

## Risk

Two-way door. A GitHub-sourced task's prompts change shape; other tasks are unchanged byte for byte. Text the model copies out of the fence is not fenced by code: the chief's wake prompts quote the task title, the chief's tool results (todos, todo, conversation) return titles and specs, and split children get their spec from the chief with `sourceKind` `orchestration`; the chief rule and the Implementer note cover these, so they rest on the model following its prompt. A paraphrase saved as memory without the marker passes the memory gate. Skill selection in `machines.ts` matches keywords on the raw text; it chooses catalog entries and puts no issue text into the brief. In the chief thread view, Markdown lazy continuation renders the footer line inside the quote; the text the model reads is not affected.

Seeding never overwrites a persona row that exists, so a team seeded before this change, the live instance included, keeps the old Implementer text until someone edits it; new teams get the new text.

The live check of the engine reading AGENTS.md in a daemon worktree, skills usable and gates running needs a long-lived host and a daemon with model credentials: 待宿主 (spec 28 §8).

`docs/verify/1406/p5-3-prompts.ts` and `p5-3-mutate.mjs` are the scripts that produced their outputs; nothing runs them. The patch is 2,429 lines (1,242 outside `docs/verify/`) across 26 files and touches `apps/server/src/services/machines.ts` (ADR 0021 D4 class ⑤), so it waits for a user merge.

## Acceptance

- [x] Issue text fenced in every path where it reaches a model in code, and absent from every system layer (`issue-fence.test.ts` in shared, server and daemon, `p5-3-prompts.txt`)
- [x] Tasks not from GitHub keep their prompts byte for byte (`issue-fence.test.ts`)

mergedPulls.title: server(1466): GitHub repo refs refuse dot segments; chief and MCP check the project's team
mergedPulls.body:
## What

Ticket #1466: two gaps found by the security pass on #1467 (P5a-2 of #1406).

- `parseGithubRepoRef` in `packages/shared/src/records/project.ts` is the one place that checks and splits `owner/repo`. It keeps the existing character set and rejects `.` and `..` as owner or repo, the only names that change a URL path when they are put in one (`repos/../user/issues` resolves to `/user/issues`). `isGithubRepoRef` is its true/false form, so POST and PATCH `/api/projects`, chief `connect_repo`, the web forms and the daemon PR probe all refuse such a value. `...`, `.github` and `my.org/repo.js` stay valid.
- `parseGithubIssueSourceRef` (`packages/shared/src/records/todo.ts`) applies the same check (and with it the `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` character set the stored repo already had), so a stored `github:../user#3` is refused by the source-issue echo and the #452 title write-back.
- `githubRepoOfProject` in `apps/server/src/services/git.ts` is the one place the server splits a stored `project.githubRepo` for an API request. A stored value that fails the check counts as "not a GitHub project" and no request is sent: the issue list and import, the #452 issue creation and retry, the CI check-runs poller, the PR state probe, and the delivery step that decides whether a build waits for CI (such a build goes to review, as in a project without a GitHub repository).
- `requireProjectRow` in `chief-tools.ts` and `mcp-face.ts` takes the caller's team and filters on it, so another team's project id gives the same 404 as a missing one. Callers: chief `docs`, `create_todo`, `update_project`, `connect_repo`, `run_builds`, `watch_todos`; MCP `create_todo`. `run_builds` and `watch_todos` check every task and its project before they start or watch anything, so a call that names another team's project changes nothing. Chief and MCP `todos` always filter on the team (another team's `projectId` lists `[]`, as a missing id does), and `watch_todos` skips another team's task as it skips a missing one.

## Verified

The new tests against unchanged sources (origin/main `2294b08`), [red.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e87699c31995f054ce0bd695cd92e169b6d49cdd/docs/verify/1466/red.txt):

```
 Test Files  3 failed (3)
      Tests  47 failed | 13 passed (60)
```

Each red case fails for the reason it names: a request to `repos/../user/...` recorded by the fake GitHub, or a call on another team's project that succeeds. The daemon probe case was added while checking callers; mutation M1, which restores the old check exactly, turns it red. Green at `18ca807` (the file names no commit; the code at `e87699c` is the same) ([green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e87699c31995f054ce0bd695cd92e169b6d49cdd/docs/verify/1466/green.txt)):

```
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  69 passed (69)
```

Eight mutations, one per rule, are each caught ([mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e87699c31995f054ce0bd695cd92e169b6d49cdd/docs/verify/1466/mutations.txt), runner [mutate.mjs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e87699c31995f054ce0bd695cd92e169b6d49cdd/docs/verify/1466/mutate.mjs), sources checked byte-identical afterwards): the dot check (37 tests fail), the source-ref check (9), `githubRepoOfProject` (10), the chief and MCP team filters (5 and 1), chief and MCP `todos` (1 each) and `watch_todos` (1).

Live, on a scratch server at `07ab360` (port 8795, scratch `PACMAN_HOME`, every outbound connection logged by a proxy on 8796), 41 checks pass ([live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e87699c31995f054ce0bd695cd92e169b6d49cdd/docs/verify/1466/live.txt)):

- POST `/api/projects` answers 400 for `../user`, `./x`, `owner/..`, `owner/.`, `../..` and `{owner: "..", repo: "user"}`, and PATCH local to github answers 400 for three of them, each with no connection to api.github.com. `my.org/repo.js`, `x/...` and `octo-org/.github` pass the check.
- With `../user`, `owner/..` and `./x` written into the database, the issue list and import answer 404 for each; for the `../user` project a new task starts no issue creation, the retry answers "project is not github-backed" and a `github:../user#1` source ref answers "source issue not found" (the other two values are covered for these paths by tests R3 and R4). The proxy log holds 6 connections, all from the control calls on valid repositories.
- Over `/api/mcp` with team A's key, `create_todo` on team B's project returns the same text as a missing id and adds nothing; `todos` with team B's `projectId` returns `[]`. Team B and the GitHub connection row were made in SQL, since one team is reachable through the API. `watch_todos` is a chief tool and is covered by `project-team-guard.test.ts`.

Gates at `18ca807` ([gates.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e87699c31995f054ce0bd695cd92e169b6d49cdd/docs/verify/1466/gates.txt)): `pnpm lint` (788 files, the existing info in `machines-page.tsx:317`), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, the spawn gate and `e2e:affected` (8 passed, port 8389 free) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` passes 2493 with the one root-only failure (`runner-brief.test.ts` "擦除失败": `chmodSync(cwd, 0o500)` does nothing for root, CI runs as a normal user). `/code-review` at low effort on `origin/main..claude/bootstrap-p5c-1466` found nothing ([reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e87699c31995f054ce0bd695cd92e169b6d49cdd/docs/verify/1466/reviews.txt)). `/security-review` (AGENTS.md lists `mcp-face.ts`) ran on `origin/HEAD...HEAD` at `07ab360` with its diff taken from this branch and found nothing at its confidence threshold ([security-review.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/e87699c31995f054ce0bd695cd92e169b6d49cdd/docs/verify/1466/security-review.txt)); `reviews.txt` records an earlier attempt whose context came from another checkout.

Round 2, after pr-gate run 1 (go at `e87699c`, suggestions only; verdict in [pr-gate-1468-run1-e87699c.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/0a4b0039833fce96e594d5c8dd47815fc167361e/docs/verify/1466/pr-gate-1468-run1-e87699c.json)), at `ab18cc3` ([r2-red-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/0a4b0039833fce96e594d5c8dd47815fc167361e/docs/verify/1466/r2-red-green.txt), [r2-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/0a4b0039833fce96e594d5c8dd47815fc167361e/docs/verify/1466/r2-mutations.txt), [gates-2.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/0a4b0039833fce96e594d5c8dd47815fc167361e/docs/verify/1466/gates-2.txt)). The run found two orderings this change got wrong. Chief `run_builds` checked the project's team after `startBuilds`, so a team-A task pointing at a team-B project (rows the earlier `create_todo` could make) started a build and then answered 404; `watch_todos` could watch earlier ids before the 404. Both now check every task first. The delivery step still read the raw `githubRepo` column, so a build delivered in a project with an invalid stored repo waited for a CI poller that now skips it; it uses `githubRepoOfProject` and goes to review. With the round 2 tests on `ddb06ca` (tests only, sources as `e87699c`) 6 of 41 fail; at `ab18cc3` 41 of 41 pass, and the wider suite passes (the run at this round was not archived; `r3-green.txt` records it at round 3). Four mutations (the project check back after `startBuilds`, checked one task at a time, the old `watch_todos` loop, the raw column) are each caught. The daemon probe test no longer asserts `https://github.com/../user.git`, which URL parsing turns into one segment on main too. Gates at `ab18cc3`: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, the spawn gate and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` passes 2498 with the one root-only failure. `/code-review` on `e87699c..0a4b003` found nothing (its output was not kept; `r3-reviews.txt` reconstructs the call).

Round 3, after pr-gate run 2 (go at `0a4b003`, suggestions only; verdict in [pr-gate-1468-run2-0a4b003.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/193e664977657ba178b3e1020a6193d0fedb7fa7/docs/verify/1466/pr-gate-1468-run2-0a4b003.json)), at `193e664` ([r3-mutations.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/193e664977657ba178b3e1020a6193d0fedb7fa7/docs/verify/1466/r3-mutations.txt), [r3-reviews.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/193e664977657ba178b3e1020a6193d0fedb7fa7/docs/verify/1466/r3-reviews.txt), [r3-green.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/193e664977657ba178b3e1020a6193d0fedb7fa7/docs/verify/1466/r3-green.txt), [gates-3.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/193e664977657ba178b3e1020a6193d0fedb7fa7/docs/verify/1466/gates-3.txt), [gates-3b.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xiechimon/pacman/193e664977657ba178b3e1020a6193d0fedb7fa7/docs/verify/1466/gates-3b.txt)). Round 2 moved R7 through `completeStep`, so the CI poller's guard for an invalid stored repo was no longer reached; R7b puts a delivered build straight into building for `../user` and `owner/..` and asserts no outbound call and one skipped candidate, and reverting the guard to main's form fails exactly those two cases. `/simplify` added one test helper (`mcpError`); the other points it raised are recorded with the reason they stay. The branch then took main at `49af6f2` (#1467) by a merge commit without conflicts, and `github-reads.ts` now gets owner and repo from `githubRepoOfProject` instead of its own split and dot check, with the same 404 and 409 answers; its bad-slug test now lists `./x`, `x/.` and `x/..`, and removing the shared dot check fails it. The wider set (the #1466 tests, github-reads, chief-dispatch, chief-watch, chief-tools, ci-loop and m4a-chief-loop) passes 165 of 165. Gates after the merge: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm spec:parse`, the spawn gate and `e2e:affected` (8 passed) exit 0; `vitest run --changed origin/main` passes 2677 with the one root-only failure. `/code-review` at low effort on the round found nothing; at that effort it read no test hunks, which the mutation runs cover.

## Upstream

No dependency. The naming rule comes from GitHub's docs ("Creating a new repository": letters, digits, `.`, `-`, `_`, at most 100 characters) and the WHATWG URL Standard (only `.`, `..` and their `%2e` forms are dot segments; `%` is outside the allowed characters). The sources are cited in `github-repo-ref.test.ts` and in the `project.ts` comment.

## Risk

Two-way door. A project whose stored `githubRepo` is `.` or `..` in either half now behaves as a project without a GitHub repository for every API read and write; such a value can no longer be stored. Same-team behavior of the chief and MCP tools is unchanged, except that chief `run_builds` with a list now refuses the whole list when one task is missing or belongs to another team's project, where before the earlier tasks were started; a call naming another team's project now gets 404 or `[]`, which matters only where a server holds more than one team.

Left as they are, recorded in `reviews.txt` and `security-review.txt`: clone URLs (`projectRepoRef`, `toProjectRecord`, the branch sync in `routes-builds.ts`) are still built from a stored invalid row; the host is fixed to github.com and the clone fails, and treating the row as unbound there would change what claimed steps receive. A task that was already stuck in building in such a project before this change stays there until a person moves it. MCP `run_builds` and the chief and MCP `schedule_todo` check the task's team but not its project's, as chief `run_builds` did before this change; chief and MCP `conversation`, chief `usage` and `save_memory` take no team check. They predate this change, reach no other team on a single-team server, and are #1470.

`docs/verify/1466/mutate.mjs` and `r2-mutate.mjs` are the mutation runners kept with their output; nothing runs them. The chief and MCP `todos` tools now filter on the team, which the ticket did not list; it only narrows what another team can read. #1467 is on main and its reads now go through `githubRepoOfProject` here. #1461 (issue intake) and #1414 (`githubTarget` in `ci-loop.ts`) still split `githubRepo` on their own; whichever of them merges after this PR routes through `githubRepoOfProject` in its merge. This branch and #1414 both change the check-runs poller in `apps/server/src/services/ci-loop.ts`, and `git merge-tree` reports a conflict there; whichever merges second takes main by a merge commit and keeps both changes. It merges cleanly with #1411, #1421, #1461 and #1467.

The patch is 3,838 lines (1,035 outside `docs/verify/`) across 36 files and touches `apps/server/src/services/mcp-face.ts` (ADR 0021 D4 class ⑤), so it waits for a user merge.

## Acceptance

- [x] `.` and `..` refused as owner or repo on every write path, and a stored one sends no GitHub request (`red.txt`, `green.txt`, `live.txt`)
- [x] `requireProjectRow` filters on the caller's team in chief and MCP; another team's project answers as a missing one (`project-team-guard.test.ts`, `live.txt`)
- [x] 8 of 8 mutations caught, 4 of 4 in round 2 and the CI poller guard in round 3 (`mutations.txt`, `r2-mutations.txt`, `r3-mutations.txt`)
- [x] `github-reads.ts` (#1467) uses `githubRepoOfProject` after the merge of main (`gates-3b.txt`)
- [x] `run_builds` and `watch_todos` refuse before changing anything; a delivery in a project with an invalid stored repo goes to review (`r2-red-green.txt`)
- [x] `/security-review` run, no finding at its threshold (`security-review.txt`)
- [x] lint / typecheck / spec:parse / vitest --changed / e2e:affected pass, except the root-only runner-brief case (`gates.txt`, `gates-2.txt`, `gates-3.txt`, `gates-3b.txt`)

## Issues

The squash message below carries the closing line for #1466. The gaps were found by the security pass on #1467 (part of #1406).

Squash with this message:

```
server(1466): GitHub repo refs refuse dot segments; chief and MCP check the project's team (#1468)

parseGithubRepoRef (shared) checks and splits owner/repo and refuses
. and .. as owner or repo; isGithubRepoRef and parseGithubIssueSourceRef
use it. The server splits a stored project.githubRepo only through
githubRepoOfProject, so an invalid stored value sends no GitHub request
(issue list and import, #452 issue creation and retry, CI check-runs,
PR state probe, delivery waiting for CI). requireProjectRow in
chief-tools and mcp-face filters on the caller's team; run_builds and
watch_todos check every task's project before changing anything; chief
and MCP todos always filter on the team. The GitHub read tools take
owner and repo from githubRepoOfProject.

closes #1466

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_012odUHNQRa4CWjzR22iWH8s
```
